{"parentUuid":"9d38ba49-b09c-430a-b833-3638c90619b6","isSidechain":false,"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/domain-modeling\n\n# Domain Modeling\n\nActively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)\n\n## File structure\n\nMost repos have a single context:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/\n│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nIf a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n├── src/\n│   ├── ordering/\n│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions\n│   └── billing/\n│       ├── CONTEXT.md\n│       └── docs/adr/\n```\n\nCreate files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.\n\n## During the session\n\n### Challenge against the glossary\n\nWhen the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. \"Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?\"\n\n### Sharpen fuzzy language\n\nWhen the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. \"You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things.\"\n\n### Discuss concrete scenarios\n\nWhen domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.\n\n### Cross-reference with code\n\nWhen the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: \"Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?\"\n\n### Update CONTEXT.md inline\n\nWhen a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).\n\n`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.\n\n### Offer ADRs sparingly\n\nOnly offer to create an ADR when all three are true:\n\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder \"why did they do it this way?\"\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\n\nIf any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).\n\n\nARGUMENTS: CONTEXT.md glossary + ADR format for the Peña Albiazul CMS grill"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"e74a27dc-c8d4-48d9-9e93-b42ee41e7231","timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:24:19.685Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01CtbiKiPLBXLihVJTL2jfmV","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"fc0bb6f4-9d23-4e4f-9aed-fc5bba24389e","isSidechain":false,"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011EJYGTZdNDLe8ACpkAykMX","type":"tool_result","content":"# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n\n## Single vs multi-context repos\n\n**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.\n\n**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n\n```md\n# Context Map\n\n## Contexts\n\n- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n\n## Relationships\n\n- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n```\n\nThe skill infers which structure applies:\n\n- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context\n- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n\nWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n=====ADR\n# ADR Format\n\nADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.\n\nCreate the `docs/adr/` directory lazily: only when the first ADR is needed.\n\n## Template\n\n```md\n# {Short title of the decision}\n\n{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}\n```\n\nThat's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why*, not in filling out sections.\n\n## Optional sections\n\nOnly include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.\n\n- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`): useful when decisions are revisited\n- **Considered Options**: only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering\n- **Consequences**: only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out\n\n## Numbering\n\nScan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.\n\n## When to offer an ADR\n\nAll three of these must be true:\n\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will look at the code and wonder \"why on earth did they do it this way?\"\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\n\nIf a decision is easy to reverse, skip it: you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond \"we did the obvious thing.\"\n\n### What qualifies\n\n- **Architectural shape.** \"We're using a monorepo.\" \"The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres.\"\n- **Integration patterns between contexts.** \"Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP.\"\n- **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library: just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.\n- **Boundary and scope decisions.** \"Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only.\" The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.\n- **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** \"We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X.\" Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from \"fixing\" something that was deliberate.\n- **Constraints not visible in the code.** \"We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements.\" \"Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract.\"\n- **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it; otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"f112fc1d-ebf8-4697-9690-04eb33834d87","timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:24:24.748Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. {"parentUuid":"73b6a9d8-b583-4ce9-88cf-b94e6ebd1395","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"3d86ff4b-cc3d-4be6-a2c9-5e111748aada","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"esto es el client brief \n\n\n<pasted_content id=\"c95a\">\n# Client brief — Club de Aficionados Albiazul\n\nUnofficial Rayados (C.F. Monterrey) fan club. Not affiliated with the club. All names and content in this project are made up.\n\n## Who runs the site\nOne fan club leader. He got the job of being the admin for the whole thing. He knows the basics on a computer, nothing technical, so the admin side has to be simple.\n\n## Who writes\nThe members. Basically any fan who wants to share their opinion about the team: how a match went, what they think of the lineup, the coach, a signing.\n\n## Who reads it, and what they want\nOther fans. They mostly want to express themselves and see what other people think. It's about opinions, not official news.\n\n## What's broken today\nRight now people post their opinions on X or Facebook. It works, but it's all mixed with everything else. I think a site just for this, just for Rayados fans, is better.\n\n## What would make it better\nOne place where the fan opinions live, organized, and easy to read.\n\n## What must never happen\nNo aggression toward other people. No threats against people or places. Trash talk toward other teams (tiraderas to Tigres, etc.) is fine, that's part of being a fan, but it can never cross into threats or attacking someone personally. That's why nothing should go public without the leader checking it first.\n</pasted_content id=\"c95a\">\n"},"uuid":"2b9c003e-c9a3-40b4-81d0-fe5762980472","timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:29:16.680Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":3,"turnIndex":3},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"type":"file-history-snapshot","messageId":"44b45b50-3e0f-4bf2-895f-f8507b6f51d2","snapshot":{"messageId":"44b45b50-3e0f-4bf2-895f-f8507b6f51d2","trackedFileBackups":{"notes/client-brief.md":{"backupFileName":"c738cfa314f07346@v2","version":2,"backupTime":"2026-10-10T17:30:49.012Z","realParentDir":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes"}},"timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:53:04.407Z"},"isSnapshotUpdate":false}
{"parentUuid":"5c1ea174-cd7a-4518-9a61-3bebc595d87e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9ee83fcd-a054-45a4-9783-1b9bb04006c2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"this is my cms thing \n\n\n<pasted_content id=\"c95a\">\n# CMS field notes — WordPress Playground\n\n1. **Quick Draft:** I wrote a quick post saying \"Rayados beat Pumas 2-1\" and saved it as a draft. I thought it might show up on the website, but it didn't. This makes sense because sometimes you want to work on a post before everyone can see it. For my fan club, this would help me prepare news before posting it.\n\n2. **Publishing the post:** After I clicked Publish, my post appeared on the website above the Hello World post. I also noticed that the text was not perfectly aligned with the title, which looked a little weird. For my fan club, I would need to check how posts look after publishing them.\n\n3. **Creating a page:** I created a page called \"Next Matches\" and it automatically appeared in the top menu. What surprised me was that regular posts don't appear there. I think this is useful because I could have pages for important information and posts for regular news and updates.\n\n4. **Page URL:** When I checked the URL, I noticed that WordPress automatically used the page title to create `/next-matches/`. This made sense and I think it's useful because fans could easily find and share different pages.\n\n5. **Footer:** I noticed that even after creating a new page, the footer links stayed exactly the same. I thought they might update automatically like the top menu, but they didn't. For my fan club, I would probably need to edit the footer separately if I wanted to add more links.\n\n6. **Creating a user:** I created a new user called fan1 and gave them the Editor role. I also noticed that WordPress showed the password strength as Medium and allowed the admin to change user roles. This would be useful for my fan club because I could have other people helping me manage the website.\n\n7. **Logging in as an Editor:** When I logged in as juan perez, I noticed that several options disappeared from the menu, like Plugins, Users, and Settings. At first I was surprised, but it makes sense because an Editor shouldn't have the same control as an admin. For my fan club, this would allow people to help with posts without changing important website settings.\n\n8. **Update notice:** Another thing I noticed was that the update message changed. As an admin, I could update WordPress, but as an Editor, it only told me to contact the administrator. This makes sense because only certain users should be able to make big changes to the website.\n\n9. **Trying to access Users:** I tried typing `/wp-admin/users.php` directly while logged in as an Editor, but WordPress didn't let me access it. I thought maybe typing the URL would work, but it still blocked me. This showed me that WordPress actually protects admin features, which is important for keeping my fan club website secure.\n</pasted_content id=\"c95a\">\n"},"uuid":"44b45b50-3e0f-4bf2-895f-f8507b6f51d2","timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:53:04.362Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":5,"turnIndex":5},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"461a00a2-de37-4be7-8bc4-86895c5c02f2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CftzK3kQaXaBxdiVGg6gx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01B5zcWntWuXDJCVU7gtTJ9M","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# Albiazul fan club CMS\n\nAn unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the club leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and the site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader returning a submitted post to draft instead of publishing it.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n### House rules\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":28,"cache_read_input_tokens":120893,"output_tokens":2883,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":2132},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":28,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2883,"cache_read_input_tokens":120893,"cache_creation_input_tokens":28,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":28},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01B5zcWntWuXDJCVU7gtTJ9M":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# Albiazul fan club CMS\n\nAn unofficial fan club of C.F. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"3612cc3d-798b-4dee-809d-c83d9bca412c","timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:57:48.053Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"update","filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# Albiazul fan club CMS\n\nAn unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the club leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and the site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader returning a submitted post to draft instead of publishing it.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n### House rules\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":3,"newStart":1,"newLines":51,"lines":["-# CONTEXT.md glossary","+# Albiazul fan club CMS"," ","-(Your /grill-with-docs session fills this in as terms are settled.)","+An unofficial fan club of C.F. {"parentUuid":"c3d96037-94d7-48e9-8eaf-cae382f26bc3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CftzMMFRf4f7YicJo6oL5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Locked in as C. `CONTEXT.md` now has its first terms, in three groups:\n\n- **People:** Leader, Member, Reader\n- **Post lifecycle:** Draft, Submitted, Published, Send back, Unpublish\n- **House rules:** *Tiradera* and *Personal attack*, taken from your brief\n\nThe heading says \"Albiazul fan club\" for now, until we settle the name.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2 - What happens when a member edits a post that's already published?**\n\nQ1 controls how a post gets *onto* the site, but a post can also change after it's there. Example: the leader publishes a member's opinion on the Clásico Regio. The next day the member opens it again and adds a line that crosses into a personal attack. If that edit saves straight to the published post, the next export ships it without the leader ever seeing it.\n\n- **A. Members can only edit drafts.** Submitting locks the post, though the member can withdraw it back to draft to fix a typo. Once it's published, only the leader can edit or unpublish it. Unpublishing returns it to draft so the member can rework it and submit again. This is how WordPress treats Contributors.\n- **B. Members can edit a published post, but saving sends it back to submitted.** It disappears from the public site until the leader approves it again, so fixing a typo takes the post offline.\n- **C. Members' edits wait as a pending revision while the old version stays live.** This is the \"revision history\" extra credit, a whole subsystem on its own.\n\n➡️ **A.** It's one rule: \"members edit drafts, nothing else.\" That's easy to enforce in code and easy to test, because an editor saving a submitted or published post gets a 403. It also never lets an unchecked edit reach the site, and it never pulls a post offline over a typo."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2969,"cache_read_input_tokens":120921,"output_tokens":713,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":133},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2969,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":713,"cache_read_input_tokens":120921,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2969,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2969},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CftzMLtbcdE5MdaFKayy1","type":"assistant","uuid":"863a5185-0d72-443d-874b-d3e9dc3cec30","timestamp":"2026-10-10T17:57:58.131Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

A reason like that is exactly what the judge counts for A1, and your last two answers were just letters.\n\nI added a new term to `CONTEXT.md`:\n\n> **Pending edit**: a member's change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays on the public site until the leader approves it. *Avoid: revision* (that word means history).\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3 - How big should pending edits be?**\n\nC opens one fork: keep only the edit that's waiting, or keep every version.\n\n- **A. Small: one pending edit per post, no history.** The rules would be:\n  1. A post has at most one pending edit. If the member saves again, the new version replaces it.\n  2. The leader's review screen shows the published version and the proposed one side by side.\n  3. **Approve** replaces the published version, and the next export ships it. **Send back** throws the pending edit away and leaves the published version untouched.\n  4. A post's slug never changes after it's first published, so links fans shared on X or Facebook keep working.\n  5. The leader's own edits go live directly, and a member can pull a *submitted* post back to draft to fix it.\n- **B. Full history.** Every approved version is kept and the leader can roll back to any of them. This is the rubric's \"Revision history with rollback\" extra credit, worth 2 points. It needs its own `stretch` issue and one more ticket, and it only counts if you already score 70 or more without it.\n\n➡️ **A.** It does everything C promised and stays one ticket. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"46a74a6e-a3db-474e-82e6-c5b44f66671b","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:00:09.464Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"**Send back**:\nThe leader returning a submitted post to draft instead of publishing it.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract","newString":"**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit**:\nA member's proposed change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve**:\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)","originalFile":"# Albiazul fan club CMS\n\nAn unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the club leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and the site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader returning a submitted post to draft instead of publishing it.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n### House rules\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":32,"oldLines":14,"newStart":32,"newLines":26,"lines":[" A post the leader has approved. {"parentUuid":"173f1477-7b82-49be-a93f-3ac0cbe81c54","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CftzXmgNfSfF9GCUAhYaT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I wrote down the A rules and added three terms to `CONTEXT.md`:\n\n- **Pending edit**, which was missing from the file even though my last message said I'd added it\n- **Withdraw**\n- **Approve**, kept separate from *publish*: the leader *publishes* a submitted post and *approves* a pending edit\n\nI also widened **Send back** so it covers both cases. The slug lock and \"the leader's own edits go live directly\" are rules for the spec, not glossary terms.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4 - What is a post?**\n\nYour three sources disagree on this:\n\n| Source | What a post is |\n|---|---|\n| First message | match report, preview, club news |\n| Client brief | \"opinions, not official news\": how a match went, the lineup, the coach, a signing. Fans want it \"organized, easy to read.\" |\n| Field notes | \"prepare news,\" \"posts for regular news and updates,\" plus a \"Next Matches\" *page* |\n\nThe options:\n\n- **A. Every post is just an opinion, with no kind or topic.** It's sorted by date only. This is the smallest build, but \"organized\" stops at newest-first.\n- **B. Every post is an opinion with exactly one topic from a fixed list.** The list comes straight from your brief: **Match**, **Lineup**, **Coach**, **Signings**, plus **Club news** for the leader's own announcements, like watch parties and meetups, which is where your field notes' \"news\" fits. Each topic gets its own listing page on the public site. The admin content list can filter by topic too. The list lives in code, so there's no screen for managing categories.\n- **C. Kinds from your first message: match report, preview, news.** This contradicts the brief's \"not official news,\" and previews mostly duplicate a Schedule page.\n- **D. Free tags or categories the leader manages.** That's the \"Categories and tags\" extra credit, which needs its own `stretch` issue and admin screens.\n\n➡️ **B.** It gives the brief's \"organized\" a concrete meaning using the brief's own list. It keeps your field notes' news without turning the site into an official news site. A fixed list costs one field and one filter. Next matches stay on a page, as in your field notes."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2319,"cache_read_input_tokens":128274,"output_tokens":854,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":145},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2319,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":854,"cache_read_input_tokens":128274,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2319,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2319},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CftzXmRjzuK52EsznFZ6a","type":"assistant","uuid":"6605ef09-e67a-4d98-9b18-d5800a2b94f3","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:00:28.405Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Not official news about C.F. Monterrey.\n_Avoid_: Official news, announcements\n\n### Post lifecycle","originalFile":"# Albiazul fan club CMS\n\nAn unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the club leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and the site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit**:\nA member's proposed change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve**:\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n### House rules\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":6,"newStart":18,"newLines":20,"lines":[" Any fan visiting the public site. {"parentUuid":"6802304b-5947-46d8-935a-da41e68085b3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CftzoDu8gxdQJ3NDXst2Y","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Spanish for everything people see, English for code, URLs, and form field names. In `CONTEXT.md`, each topic now carries its Spanish label (*Partido, Alineación, Técnico, Fichajes, Noticias del club de aficionados*), and there's a new **Disclaimer** term for the line saying the site is unofficial, in Spanish with your English line underneath.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7 - How does a fan become a member?**\n\nThe public site is static files on GitHub Pages, so it can't host a sign-up form. Nothing there can receive one. That means every account is created by hand by the leader. What's still open is how a fan asks to join, and what happens to the password.\n\nMy proposed setup:\n\n1. The leader creates the account in the admin console with an email to log in with, the name shown on posts, the role, and a temporary password. The test helper in `tests/conftest.py` already logs in by email.\n2. The **How to Join** page on the public site tells fans how to ask. **You need to supply this part: how do fans reach the leader today?** For example a WhatsApp group, an Instagram DM, an email address, or asking in person at a watch party.\n3. Every user can change their own password after their first login, so the leader doesn't keep knowing everyone's password.\n\nThe alternative is to skip step 3, keep the build smaller, and have the leader set and reset all passwords. That's weak, because your brief says \"any fan\" can join, so the leader would end up holding a lot of passwords.\n\n➡️ **Steps 1–3 as written**, with the contact method from you. {"parentUuid":"c8545751-3566-4df3-98da-401947bf167f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CftzxbepNTgYccwRQpLMb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Happy to pin it down. I can read your answer three ways, and they behave very differently.\n\n**(a) A sign-up screen.** A fan opens a \"Create account\" page, picks a username and password, and the account exists.\n```\nfan → [Crear cuenta: usuario / contraseña] → account created\n```\nThere are two problems. First, the public site is plain files on GitHub Pages, so it can't save an account; the only place a sign-up page could live is the admin console on the leader's laptop. Second, capability 6 in the rubric says **\"admin only: create users.\"** A screen where fans create their own accounts breaks that rule.\n\n**(b) One shared login.** Every member uses the same username and password, and all posts live inside that one account.\n```\n[usuario: albiazul / contraseña: ****] ← everyone uses this\n```\nThis breaks capabilities 3 and 6. Posts would have no real author, and the leader couldn't deactivate one person without locking out everyone. It also breaks your brief: if someone posts a personal attack, the leader can't tell who wrote it.\n\n**(c) One leader account at the top, everyone else under it.** The leader's account is the only one that can create accounts. He creates one for each member, each with their own username and password.\n```\nLeader (admin)\n ├── member 1 (own username + password)\n ├── member 2 (own username + password)\n └── member 3 ...\n```\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7 (clarified) - Which of these did you mean?**\n\n➡️ **(c).** It fits your \"one user, and all the other users under it.\" It meets the rubric's \"admin only: create users.\" The leader also always knows who wrote what, which is the whole point of your *must never happen* section.\n\nIf you meant (a) because you don't want the leader typing in every account, say so. There's a version where a fan's sign-up only creates a *request* that the leader has to switch on. It costs more and stretches the rubric, but it's doable."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":100,"cache_read_input_tokens":141528,"output_tokens":2223,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1603},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":100,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2223,"cache_read_input_tokens":141528,"cache_creation_input_tokens":100,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":100},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CftzxawA7Ztwfhf1Q3yLv","type":"assistant","uuid":"ee3331c3-ea9f-411a-a8c8-d942353ac643","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:06:11.275Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"240a2748-bcf5-4827-8838-7b75e8e5c3b5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu1CSFfrXD9TovxRGag2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Going with B: members can see every post but can only edit or delete their own, and only while it's a draft. Here's what that means in practice, for the spec:\n\n- Every member's content list shows all posts, and they can filter it. On other members' posts there are no edit or delete buttons.\n- The rule is enforced on the server, not by hiding buttons. If a member sends an edit or delete for someone else's post directly, they get a **403**. That's checklist item #10, and it's what your field note 9 noticed WordPress doing.\n- Page screens stay leader-only, because B covers posts, not pages.\n\nThe trade-off you accepted is that a draft the leader would never publish can still be read by other members. That's worth one sentence in your report.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q10 - What do readers see on a post, and whose name is on it?**\n\nEvery post stores its author, which the rubric requires. What's still open is the name readers see on the public site.\n\n- **A. A nickname the leader assigns,** like \"El Güero de Cumbres,\" shown on every post along with the topic and the publish date. If the leader approves a pending edit, the post also shows \"Actualizado el…\". Only the leader knows the real person behind the nickname, through the account email. Members can't change their own display name, so one member can't rename themselves to look like another.\n- **B. Real first name and last initial,** like \"Diego R.\" It's more accountable in public and less like how fans actually post.\n- **C. No name on public posts.** Everything appears under \"Club de Aficionados Albiazul,\" and the author only shows up in the admin console. It's the safest option, but then the site doesn't show \"what other people think,\" which is what your brief says readers come for.\n\n➡️ **A.** It works like X and Facebook, where your fans post now: under a handle. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Reader**:","originalFile":"# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post**:\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page**:\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit**:\nA member's proposed change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve**:\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":24,"oldLines":6,"newStart":24,"newLines":10,"lines":[" A fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Their real identity is known only to the leader.","+_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias","+"," **Reader**:"," Any fan visiting the public site. {"parentUuid":"10558254-4984-43af-9762-fad3f86c3494","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4bf6169e-13d2-46ea-82b7-b10846c61346","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NZhkgLw2xXVLZQUdgxBpww","type":"tool_result","content":"# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts, chosen by that person. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post**:\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page**:\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft**:\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted**:\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published**:\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back**:\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish**:\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next export.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit**:\nA member's proposed change to a published post, waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve**:\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"45a12e47-a63e-4fdb-a522-2c85488213dd","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:11:03.106Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. {"parentUuid":"b8360f7e-5ff3-4e69-ac37-62cb5b76dd3c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu1S14k1NCoHe6Lvg2gk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Going with C, plus three details I added:\n\n- **Nicknames are unique,** so nobody can take another member's.\n- **Mi cuenta** shows the nickname read-only and changes only the password.\n- **The seeded demo users already have nicknames.** The judge logs in as the seeded editor, and a \"choose your nickname\" screen in the way could break their scripted walkthrough.\n\n`CONTEXT.md` now records that the nickname is chosen once and only the leader changes it after that.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q12 - How does the leader put changes on the internet?**\n\nClicking *Publish* in the admin console only changes a post's status in the database. Readers see nothing until someone **exports** the site (`uv run cms publish`) and **deploys** it to GitHub Pages (`uv run cms deploy`). Both are terminal commands, and your brief says the leader \"knows the basics on a computer, nothing technical.\" The rubric requires the `cms publish` command to exist no matter what.\n\n- **A. Terminal only.** The leader types both commands. It's the minimum the rubric asks for, and it doesn't fit your leader.\n- **B. A leader-only \"Actualizar el sitio\" button in the admin console** that runs the same export and deploy. It then shows what happened, for example: \"Sitio generado ✓ · Subido a GitHub ✓,\" or a plain error if the upload fails. The dashboard shows when the site was last updated. The terminal commands stay for the rubric and the judge.\n- **C. A button that only exports,** with deploying left in the terminal. It goes halfway, and the leader still opens a terminal.\n- **D. Automatic.** Every publish, approval, or unpublish triggers an export and an upload. Nothing is forgotten, but it means a GitHub push on every click, it's slow, and it's surprising when something goes wrong.\n\n➡️ **B.** It matches what your brief says about the leader. The rubric still gets its command, and since the judge's container can't push to your repo, the button simply reports that the upload failed while the export still succeeds. It also gives the glossary a clean split: *publish* is the status change, and *Actualizar el sitio* is the moment readers see it."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":28,"cache_read_input_tokens":155413,"output_tokens":2274,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1560},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":28,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2274,"cache_read_input_tokens":155413,"cache_creation_input_tokens":28,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":28},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfu1RzjtdB9UTcCq85rkz","type":"assistant","uuid":"67aa2eda-8b58-44f6-9033-17584278c5e4","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:12:25.370Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"f3ab186b-9e5d-4b49-9db9-6d12e50d999b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu1dJVJDFRrEUqQhnudv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Going with B: one section per topic on the home page, each showing its newest 3 posts. Two details to make it work:\n\n- **Each section ends with a \"Ver todos\" link** to that topic's own page. Otherwise posts older than the newest 3 would be unreachable, which would fail F2's broken-link check.\n- **A topic with no published posts is hidden,** and the demo data will include at least one published post per topic so the home page never looks empty.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q14 - Do these defaults hold?**\n\nThese are the remaining small decisions. Rather than asking each one separately, here's what I'd put in the spec. Veto any of them by number, ideally with a reason, since that counts for A1.\n\n**Posts and pages**\n1. **Slug:** built from the title with the accents removed, e.g. *\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\"* → `cronica-del-clasico-regio`. If it's already taken, a number is added. It can be edited until the post is first published, and then it's locked (Q3).\n2. **Topic and the leader's posts:** a topic is required on every post. The leader's own posts skip *submitted*, so he publishes his drafts directly.\n3. **Preview:** a **Vista previa** button in the editor shows the cleaned-up result under the form without saving. It goes through the same cleaning step as the exported site, so the preview is exactly what readers will get.\n4. **Deleting:** it always asks for confirmation. Members can only delete their own drafts; the leader can delete anything.\n\n**People**\n5. **No lockout:** the leader can't deactivate himself or take away his own admin role. He can promote a member to admin, which covers the rubric's \"change a role.\"\n6. **Deactivating, not deleting:** users are never deleted, only deactivated. Their posts stay up under their nickname, and anything they had submitted stays in the queue for the leader to decide on.\n7. **Login error:** a wrong email and a wrong password get the same message, *\"Correo o contraseña incorrectos,\"* so nobody can find out which accounts exist.\n\n**Admin console**\n8. **Dashboard:** counts of drafts, submitted, published, pending edits, pages, and active members, plus the time of the last site update.\n9. **Content list:** filters by status and topic, and the leader can also filter posts vs. pages.\n10. **Menu and messages:** the admin menu is always visible, and every save shows a success or error message (F4).\n\n**Public site**\n11. **Look:** blue and white, with no crest, logos, or photos. The disclaimer on every page reads *\"Sitio de aficionados. Sin afiliación con el Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"* with *\"Fan site, not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"* underneath.\n\n**Demo data, all fictional**\n12. **Seed contents:** the leader and two members, all with nicknames; at least one published post per topic, including one obvious tiradera aimed at Tigres; one draft, one submitted post, and one pending edit; and all four pages published.\n\n**Out of scope for v1:** comments and likes (readers only read), photo uploads, live scores and stats, multiple clubs, self sign-up, revision history, search, scheduled publishing, and pages listing each fan's posts.\n\n**Accepted limitation:** the admin console runs only on the leader's laptop (ADR-001), so in v1 members write there. Giving members remote access is the \"live admin deploy\" extra credit, and it goes first in the report's \"what next.\"\n\n**One ADR to offer: ADR-003, \"Everything readers see passes through the leader.\"** It would cover the submitted status, pending edits, the nickname lock, and members seeing other posts without touching them. It meets all three tests for an ADR:\n- **Hard to reverse:** it shapes the database and the permission check on every route.\n- **Surprising:** a future reader will ask why members can't just edit their own published post.\n- **A real trade-off:** you chose it over simpler options in Q1, Q2, and Q11.\n\n➡️ **Accept all 12 defaults and the out-of-scope list, and write ADR-003.** After that the grill is finished: you run `/to-spec`, and I'll also save the spec as `docs/tech-spec_web-cms_v1_opus-high_20261010.md`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":28,"cache_read_input_tokens":160066,"output_tokens":5119,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":3719},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":28,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5119,"cache_read_input_tokens":160066,"cache_creation_input_tokens":28,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":28},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfu1dJ4jtE6HDqLaHRTYk","type":"assistant","uuid":"a8ddb7e7-1eca-4fae-911b-b2a455b6340e","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:15:25.090Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Item 1 is now:\n\n> **Slug:** built from the title, keeping accents and ñ, e.g. *\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\"* → `crónica-del-clásico-regio`. If it's already taken, a number is added. It can be edited until the post is first published, then it's locked.\n\nSpanish Wikipedia does the same thing (`.../wiki/Club_de_Fútbol_Monterrey`), so it's fine on the web. The spec will include two safeguards so accents can't break anything:\n\n- **Letters are normalized.** An \"ó\" can be stored in two different ways that look identical. Without normalizing, the same title could produce two different slugs.\n- **Links are written in encoded form** (`cr%C3%B3nica-…`). The browser still shows the accents in the address bar, and the judge's broken-link crawler (F2) can't trip over them.\n\nThe publish tests will push an accented title through the export and check that its link works.\n\n**2–10 and 12:** locked in.\n\n**11, the look.** Here's my plan, since you left it to me:\n\n- **Stripes:** a navy-and-white striped band across the top of every public page. *Rayados* literally means \"striped,\" so the stripes say Rayados without using anything official.\n- **Cerro de la Silla:** a silhouette of the mountain in a large banner at the top of the home page, so you can tell the site is from Monterrey at a glance.\n- **Stadium:** a generic stadium silhouette above the disclaimer at the bottom of the page. It won't be labelled \"Estadio BBVA,\" because BBVA is a bank's trademark.\n- **No photos or logos:** the drawings are original vector images written straight into the page, so there are no photos, logos, or crest, and no image files to upload.\n- **Disclaimer:** it stays exactly as agreed, on every page.\n- **Admin console:** same colors, but calmer and plain, because your brief says the leader needs it simple.\n- **Phone width:** everything scales down to 390 px with no sideways scrolling (F3).\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q15 - Last check before the grill is finished**\n\nYou didn't comment on these three:\n\n1. **The out-of-scope list:** comments and likes, photo uploads, live scores and stats, multiple clubs, self sign-up, revision history, search, scheduled publishing, and per-fan pages.\n2. **The accepted limitation:** in v1 the admin console runs only on the leader's laptop, so members write there. Remote access goes first in the report's \"what next.\"\n3. **ADR-003, \"Everything readers see passes through the leader\":** it covers the submitted status, pending edits, the nickname lock, and members seeing other posts without touching them.\n\n➡️ **Yes to all three.** Then I'll write ADR-003 and the grill is finished, and you run `/to-spec`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":167,"cache_read_input_tokens":165213,"output_tokens":3050,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":2120},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":167,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3050,"cache_read_input_tokens":165213,"cache_creation_input_tokens":167,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":167},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfu26cS3xAe4HAH2z2ekC","type":"assistant","uuid":"1e6e9048-d2dd-4e75-843d-ce06ad7914d5","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:21:15.386Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"0ce5435f-d547-45a9-ae4a-db75ab2785c7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu2ELcWvwyMsTQbW3iD4","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QLfBdqPDGZBqe9hRpmEsg7","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-leader-gates-everything-public.md","content":"# ADR-003: Everything readers can see passes through the leader\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-10\n\n## Context\n\nThe client brief has one hard rule: no aggression toward people and no threats\nagainst people or places may ever go public. Trash talk toward rival clubs\n(*tiradera*) is fine. The leader's check is the only safeguard, so any path by\nwhich a member's words reach readers without that check breaks the brief.\n\nThe obvious CMS designs each leave such a path: two statuses only (the leader\ncannot tell a finished post from a half-written one), authors editing their own\npublished posts (the change ships at the next site update unseen), and display\nnames editable at any time (a rename reprints unchecked text on every past post).\n\n## Decision\n\n- Posts move **draft → submitted → published**. Members cannot publish; the\n  leader publishes a submitted post or sends it back to draft. A member may\n  withdraw their own submitted post to draft.\n- A member's change to their own published post becomes a **pending edit** (at\n  most one per post). You run **`/to-tickets`**. It creates the 7–9 ticket issues, and you check the list once.\n\nThe building happens after that, one ticket per fresh session (`/clear` → `/implement #N`). Those are the stretches where you can leave the computer. I'll tell you clearly when each one starts and when it needs you back, for the code-review comment and the commit.\n\n---\n\n**Point 2, explained more simply.** The CMS has two halves:\n\n- **The public site**, meaning the pages fans read. It goes on the internet through GitHub Pages, and anyone can open it from their phone.\n- **The admin console**, meaning the login, the writing screens, and the leader's buttons. The assignment requires that it **never goes on the internet**. It only works on the computer where someone starts it, which in your story is the leader's laptop.\n\nSo in real life, a member who wants to write a post has to sit at the leader's laptop. For the class it makes no difference, because the grader runs everything on one computer. It's still a real weakness for your client, and the report should say so.\n\n❓ **Q16 - How do you want to handle that?**\n\n- **A. {"parentUuid":"794c641a-cd78-4feb-8057-e2922a5aa9d2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu2WgeyJWWShipLbEVtP","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Yes, that's right. In v1 no member can write from their own phone or computer, only at the leader's laptop.\n\nYour hybrid idea is good, and it's yours: the leader's powers (publishing, users, *Actualizar el sitio*) stay on the laptop, and only \"write a post and submit it to the leader\" goes online. That puts much less online than a full live admin console would. It still needs a small server, because GitHub Pages can only show files; it can't receive anything. I'll put it in the spec as the planned next step and credit it to you. Write it in your own words in the report's \"what next\" section too, since that's the kind of specific detail A3 rewards.\n\nTwo last edge cases I'll put in the spec unless you object:\n- **Unpublishing a post with a pending edit waiting:** the leader has to approve or send back the edit first, so the member's work isn't silently thrown away.\n- **Reserved names:** a page can't take a name the site already uses, like the home page or a topic page.\n\n---\n\n**What we agreed:**\n- **A post** is a fan's opinion under one of five fixed topics. It goes draft → submitted → published, and changes to a published post wait as a pending edit.\n- **A page** is fixed fan-club information in the menu, written only by the leader.\n- **Who can do what:** the leader (admin) handles posts, pages, users, and *Actualizar el sitio*. Members (editors) write their own posts, see everyone's, and choose a nickname once.\n- **Publishing** changes a status. Readers only see the change after the leader's *Actualizar el sitio* button, or `cms publish` plus `cms deploy`, puts it online.\n- **Out of scope:** comments and likes, photos, live scores and stats, multiple clubs, self sign-up, revision history, search, scheduled publishing, per-fan pages, and members writing from their own devices.\n\n❓ **Is that our shared understanding?** If yes, the grill is finished. There's one step before `/to-spec`:\n\n1. Run **`/setup-matt-pocock-skills`**. Part 1.4 of the manual expected it, it was never run, and `/to-spec` refuses to work without it. Answer **GitHub**, **default labels**, **single context**.\n2. Run **`/to-spec`**. {"parentUuid":"0782fedd-b565-4a04-a57b-536735980ac4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu2pcmJuHMEcJkVK7j4P","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Fair enough. For your fan club, writing from a phone is the point. Then phone writing goes in the plan, but there's one decision about *how*, because it changes three things:\n\n- **It needs a server on the internet.** Today the server only runs on a laptop, and GitHub Pages can't take the job because it only shows files. That means picking a hosting service. Most hosts that keep a database file need a paid plan or a credit card, and choosing one is your call.\n- **It breaks a hard rule in `CLAUDE.md`** (\"the admin console never goes on the public internet\") and part of ADR-001. The assignment allows exactly this only as the extra-credit **\"live admin deploy,\"** behind a security gate: admin password from an environment variable, rate-limited login, HTTPS, and no default accounts.\n- **The judge grades the local version.** They run your app on their own computer from a clean clone, so the online server earns nothing in C. It's worth the 2 extra-credit points, plus your client actually being able to use it.\n\nYour split (members online, leader on the laptop) would mean **two databases** that have to stay in sync, which is the most expensive option. It's simpler to put the whole console online: one database, and the leader can approve posts from his phone too, which suits him.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q17 - When does phone writing get built?**\n\n- **A. Plan it now and build it as a `stretch` ticket right after the 7 core tickets.** The whole console goes online with the security gate, and we pick the host when we get to that ticket. The local version stays exactly what the judge expects, and the code is written so going online is a deploy step, not a rewrite.\n- **B. Make it core from ticket 1, with every ticket deploying to the server.** Your client gets it sooner, but if the hosting has problems they block everything, and you're already past the deadline.\n- **C. Keep your split:** member writing online and the leader's powers on the laptop, with two databases kept in sync. It's the most work of the three.\n\n➡️ **A.** The grade comes from the local version, so that has to be finished first. Planning phone writing now means the spec and tickets are built around it, so it isn't an afterthought. If you pick A or B, I'll write ADR-004 (online console behind the security gate) and update the hard rule in `CLAUDE.md` to match."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":51,"cache_read_input_tokens":180952,"output_tokens":3556,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":2810},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":51,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3556,"cache_read_input_tokens":180952,"cache_creation_input_tokens":51,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":51},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfu2pcPUu3cmhYwp9cJB3","type":"assistant","uuid":"09a098b4-b7d9-48e3-b8e4-181c292cfaa1","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:30:50.804Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}
