{"parentUuid":"7f7eb3a9-28d6-4a98-b298-1dfecffb336a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu2v71pXgHEMDEUV7pFJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0155u2JDPxZRcbdWWrYQg88N","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-004-online-console-stretch.md","content":"# ADR-004: Members write from their phones through an online admin console (stretch)\n\n**Status:** accepted — takes effect with the live-admin-deploy stretch ticket.\nUntil that ticket lands, ADR-001 applies unchanged.\n**Date:** 2026-10-10\n\n## Context\n\nADR-001 keeps the admin console on one laptop, so members could only write at\nthe leader's computer. For this fan club that defeats the purpose: fans share\nopinions from their phones, the way they do today on X and Facebook. GitHub\nPages serves files only, so writing from a phone needs a server on the internet.\nThe rubric allows this only as the \"live admin deploy\" stretch goal, behind a\nsecurity gate, and the judge grades the local version.\n\n## Decision\n\nAfter the seven core tickets, a stretch ticket deploys the whole admin console,\nwith its one database, to a hosted server behind the rubric's security gate:\nadmin password from an environment variable, rate-limited login, HTTPS, and no\ndefault accounts. Members and the leader both use it from any device; accounts\nare still created only by the leader. The public site stays on GitHub Pages, and\n*Actualizar el sitio* pushes to it from the server. The local console keeps\nworking unchanged for grading. The host is chosen in that ticket.\n\n## Considered options\n\n- Members online, the leader's powers kept on the laptop — rejected for v1: two\n  databases that must stay in sync.\n- Members keep writing only on the leader's laptop — rejected: the client\n  considers the site pointless without phone writing.\n- Go online from the first ticket — rejected: grading runs the local version,\n  and hosting trouble would block core work.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The `CLAUDE.md` hard rule \"the admin console never goes on the public\n  internet\" is amended in the stretch ticket, not before, so core tickets do not\n  loosen it early.\n- Core code reads every secret and setting from the environment and assumes\n  nothing about running on localhost, so going online is a deploy step, not a\n  rewrite.\n- The server holds a GitHub token to push the public site; it is a secret.\n- Hosting with a persistent database usually needs a paid plan or a credit card.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":469,"cache_read_input_tokens":187167,"output_tokens":1003,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":178},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":469,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1003,"cache_read_input_tokens":187167,"cache_creation_input_tokens":469,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":469},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_0155u2JDPxZRcbdWWrYQg88N":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-004-online-console-stretch.md","content":"# ADR-004: Members write from their phones through an online admin console (stretch)\n\n**Status:** accepted — takes effect with the live-admin-deploy stretch ticket.\nUntil that ticket lands, ADR-001 applies unchanged.\n**Date:** 2026-10-10\n\n## Context\n\nADR-001 keeps the admin console on one laptop, so members could only write at\nthe leader's computer. For this fan club that defeats the purpose: fans share\nopinions from their phones, the way they do today on X and Facebook. GitHub\nPages serves files only, so writing from a phone needs a server on the internet.\nThe rubric allows this only as the \"live admin deploy\" stretch goal, behind a\nsecurity gate, and the judge grades the local version.\n\n## Decision\n\nAfter the seven core tickets, a stretch ticket deploys the whole admin console,\nwith its one database, to a hosted server behind the rubric's security gate:\nadmin password from an environment variable, rate-limited login, HTTPS, and no\ndefault accounts. Members and the leader both use it from any device; accounts\nare still created only by the leader. The public site stays on GitHub Pages, and\n*Actualizar el sitio* pushes to it from the server. The local console keeps\nworking unchanged for grading. The host is chosen in that ticket.\n\n## Considered options\n\n- Members online, the leader's powers kept on the laptop — rejected for v1: two\n  databases that must stay in sync.\n- Members keep writing only on the leader's laptop — rejected: the client\n  considers the site pointless without phone writing.\n- Go online from the first ticket — rejected: grading runs the local version,\n  and hosting trouble would block core work.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The `CLAUDE.md` hard rule \"the admin console never goes on the public\n  internet\" is amended in the stretch ticket, not before, so core tickets do not\n  loosen it early.\n- Core code reads every secret and setting from the environment and assumes\n  nothing about running on localhost, so going online is a deploy step, not a\n  rewrite.\n- The server holds a GitHub token to push the public site; it is a secret.\n- Hosting with a persistent database usually needs a paid plan or a credit card.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfu2v6jwrWMD53GjAZu94","type":"assistant","uuid":"b7e60a2d-12af-48ec-ab31-bc807459841b","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:31:35.983Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

For this fan club that defeats the purpose: fans share","-opinions from their phones, the way they do today on X and Facebook. GitHub","-Pages serves files only, so writing from a phone needs a server on the internet.","-The rubric allows this only as the \"live admin deploy\" stretch goal, behind a","-security gate, and the judge grades the local version.","-","-## Decision","-","-After the seven core tickets, a stretch ticket deploys the whole admin console,","-with its one database, to a hosted server behind the rubric's security gate:","-admin password from an environment variable, rate-limited login, HTTPS, and no","-default accounts. Members and the leader both use it from any device; accounts","-are still created only by the leader. The public site stays on GitHub Pages, and","-*Actualizar el sitio* pushes to it from the server. The local console keeps","-working unchanged for grading. The host is chosen in that ticket.","-","-## Considered options","-","-- Members online, the leader's powers kept on the laptop — rejected for v1: two","-  databases that must stay in sync.","-- Members keep writing only on the leader's laptop — rejected: the client","-  considers the site pointless without phone writing.","-- Go online from the first ticket — rejected: grading runs the local version,","-  and hosting trouble would block core work.","-","-## Consequences","-","-- The `CLAUDE.md` hard rule \"the admin console never goes on the public","-  internet\" is amended in the stretch ticket, not before, so core tickets do not","-  loosen it early.","-- Core code reads every secret and setting from the environment and assumes","-  nothing about running on localhost, so going online is a deploy step, not a","-  rewrite.","-- The server holds a GitHub token to push the public site; it is a secret.","-- Hosting with a persistent database usually needs a paid plan or a credit card."]}],"deleted":true}],"moreFiles":0,"changedFiles":["/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-004-online-console-stretch.md"]}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b5f614d3-cfad-4155-aae1-ad334f1bb24a","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"2bf3f455-abe3-48cb-9748-f438e4c1492f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dc45540f-1ee6-4fa3-ba87-2a42c8ae2de6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills\n\n# Setup Matt Pocock's Skills\n\nScaffold the per-repo configuration that the engineering skills assume:\n\n- **Issue tracker**: where issues live (GitHub by default; local markdown is also supported out of the box)\n- **Triage labels**: the strings used for the five canonical triage roles\n- **Domain docs**: where `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs live, and the consumer rules for reading them\n\nThis is a prompt-driven skill, not a deterministic script. Explore, present what you found, confirm with the user, then write.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Explore\n\nLook at the current repo to understand its starting state. Read whatever exists; don't assume:\n\n- `git remote -v` and `.git/config`: is this a GitHub repo? Which one?\n- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root: does either exist? Is there already an `## Agent skills` section in either?\n- `CONTEXT.md` and `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root\n- `docs/adr/` and any `src/*/docs/adr/` directories\n- `docs/agents/`: does this skill's prior output already exist?\n- `.scratch/`: a sign that a local-markdown issue tracker convention is already in use\n- Is the `triage` skill installed? (a `triage` skill folder alongside this one, or `triage` in your available skills.) This decides whether Section B runs at all.\n- Monorepo signals: a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, a `workspaces` field in `package.json`, or a populated `packages/*` with its own `src/`. These are present only in a genuinely large multi-package repo; their absence means single-context, which is almost every repo.\n\n### 2. Present findings and ask\n\nSummarise what's present and what's missing. Then take the sections in order. One section, one answer, then the next.\n\nLead each section with the recommended answer so the user can accept it in a word. Give a one-line explainer only when the choice genuinely branches; skip the section entirely when exploration already settled it (Section B when `triage` isn't installed, Section C when there's no monorepo).\n\n**Section A: Issue tracker.**\n\n> Explainer: The \"issue tracker\" is where issues live for this repo. Skills like `to-tickets`, `triage`, and `to-spec` read from and write to it. They need to know whether to call `gh issue create`, write a markdown file under `.scratch/`, or follow some other workflow you describe. Pick the place you actually track work for this repo.\n\nDefault posture: these skills were designed for GitHub. If a `git remote` points at GitHub, propose that. If a `git remote` points at GitLab (`gitlab.com` or a self-hosted host), propose GitLab. Otherwise (or if the user prefers), offer:\n\n- **GitHub**: issues live in the repo's GitHub Issues (uses the `gh` CLI)\n- **GitLab**: issues live in the repo's GitLab Issues (uses the [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) CLI)\n- **Local markdown**: issues live as files under `.scratch/<feature>/` in this repo (good for solo projects or repos without a remote)\n- **Other** (Jira, Linear, etc.): ask the user to describe the workflow in one paragraph; the skill will record it as freeform prose\n\nRecord the choice in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. The GitHub and GitLab templates carry a \"PRs as a request surface\" flag, defaulted **off**. Leave it off and don't raise it: a user who wants external PRs in the triage queue can flip the flag in the file later.\n\n**Section B: Triage label vocabulary.** Skip this section entirely if the `triage` skill isn't installed (exploration told you), since an uninstalled skill needs no labels.\n\nIf it is installed, ask exactly one question:\n\n> Do you want to keep the default triage labels? (recommended: **yes**)\n\nThe defaults are the five canonical roles, each label string equal to its name: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. On **yes**, write them as-is. Only if the user says no, usually because their tracker already uses other names (e.g. `bug:triage` for `needs-triage`), collect the overrides so `triage` applies existing labels instead of creating duplicates.\n\n**Section C: Domain docs.** Default to **single-context** (one `CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/` at the repo root). This fits almost every repo; write it without asking.\n\nOffer **multi-context** (a root `CONTEXT-MAP.md` pointing to per-context `CONTEXT.md` files) only when exploration found monorepo signals. Then confirm which layout they want.\n\n### 3. Confirm and edit\n\nShow the user a draft of:\n\n- The `## Agent skills` block to add to whichever of `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` is being edited (see step 4 for selection rules)\n- The contents of `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, `docs/agents/domain.md`, and `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` (the last only when `triage` is installed)\n\nLet them edit before writing.\n\n### 4. Write\n\n**Pick the file to edit:**\n\n- If `CLAUDE.md` exists, edit it.\n- Else if `AGENTS.md` exists, edit it.\n- If neither exists, ask the user which one to create; don't pick for them.\n\nNever create `AGENTS.md` when `CLAUDE.md` already exists (or vice versa); always edit the one that's already there.\n\nIf an `## Agent skills` block already exists in the chosen file, update its contents in-place rather than appending a duplicate. Don't overwrite user edits to the surrounding sections.\n\nThe block:\n\n```markdown\n## Agent skills\n\n### Issue tracker\n\n[one-line summary of where issues are tracked]. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n\n### Triage labels\n\n[one-line summary of the label vocabulary]. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.\n\n### Domain docs\n\n[one-line summary of layout: \"single-context\" or \"multi-context\"]. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.\n```\n\nInclude the `### Triage labels` sub-block, and write `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`, only when `triage` is installed and Section B ran. When it isn't, both are omitted.\n\nThen write the docs files using the seed templates in this skill folder as a starting point:\n\n- [issue-tracker-github.md](./issue-tracker-github.md): GitHub issue tracker\n- [issue-tracker-gitlab.md](./issue-tracker-gitlab.md): GitLab issue tracker\n- [issue-tracker-local.md](./issue-tracker-local.md): local-markdown issue tracker\n- [triage-labels.md](./triage-labels.md): label mapping (only if `triage` is installed)\n- [domain.md](./domain.md): domain doc consumer rules + layout\n\nFor \"other\" issue trackers, write `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` from scratch using the user's description.\n\n### 5. Done\n\nTell the user the setup is complete and which engineering skills will now read from these files. Mention they can edit `docs/agents/*.md` directly later; re-running this skill is only necessary if they want to switch issue trackers or restart from scratch.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"b09da230-5ae5-48ee-9876-c075e31d881c","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:32:44.470Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n===== triage-labels.md\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.\n\nIf any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't drift to synonyms the glossary explicitly avoids.","+","+If the concept you need isn't in the glossary yet, that's a signal: either you're inventing language the project doesn't use (reconsider) or there's a real gap (note it for `/domain-modeling`).","+","+## Flag ADR conflicts","+","+If your output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding:","+","+> _Contradicts ADR-0007 (event-sourced orders), but worth reopening because…_"]}],"created":true},{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/agents/issue-tracker.md","hunks":[{"oldStart":0,"oldLines":0,"newStart":1,"newLines":53,"lines":["+# Issue tracker: GitHub","+","+Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.","+","+## Conventions","+","+- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.","+- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.","+- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.","+- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`","+- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`","+- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`","+","+Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.","+","+## Pull requests as a triage surface","+","+**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_","+","+When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:","+","+- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.","+- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).","+- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.","+","+GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.","+","+## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"","+","+Create a GitHub issue.","+","+## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"","+","+Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.","+","+## Wayfinding operations","+","+Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.","+","+- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.","+- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.","+- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.","+- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.","+- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.","+- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.","+","+## Course conventions (IPHS 400 MP2 rubric)","+","+These labels are graded and sit alongside the triage labels above.","+","+- **Spec**: exactly one issue labelled `spec` (plus `ready-for-agent`). It must be created before any ticket.","+- **Tickets**: core tickets are labelled `ticket`, extra-credit tickets `stretch` (plus `ready-for-agent`). Every ticket body has an **Acceptance criteria** section and a literal `Blocked by: #N, #M` line (or `Blocked by: none`), even when native GitHub dependencies are also set.","+- **Closing a ticket**: post the `/code-review` findings and how each was resolved as a comment on the issue *before* closing it; the closing commit message starts `T0N:` and ends `Closes #N`."]}],"created":true},{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/agents/triage-labels.md","hunks":[{"oldStart":0,"oldLines":0,"newStart":1,"newLines":15,"lines":["+# Triage Labels","+","+The skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.","+","+| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |","+| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |","+| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |","+| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |","+| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |","+| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |","+| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |","+","+When a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.","+","+Edit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use."]}],"created":true}],"moreFiles":0,"changedFiles":["/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CLAUDE.md","/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/agents/domain.md","/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/agents/issue-tracker.md","/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/agents/triage-labels.md"]}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1ad253d7-2c80-4dc1-aaeb-2ead9f59d705","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

See `docs/agents/domain.md`.\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}
