{"parentUuid":"a69c230d-9797-4496-992b-5eb519787c13","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6a387353-bf90-400f-9cfc-3df9f2d88ed8","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FJHX2yQwCUHB9frnTbnbw8","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/tech-spec_web-cms_v1_opus-high_20261010.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"6069bd55-54ff-4f21-959b-9d16722c0061","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:36:55.348Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/tech-spec_web-cms_v1_opus-high_20261010.md","content":"# Spec: Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS (v1)\n\n*Source: the grill session of 2026-10-10 (`/grill-with-docs`, questions Q1–Q17). Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`; decisions respect ADR-001, ADR-002 and ADR-003.*\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nClub de Aficionados Albiazul is an unofficial fan club of Rayados (C.F. Monterrey). Its fans share opinions about the team (how a match went, the lineup, the coach, a signing), but today they post them on X and Facebook, where they are mixed in with everything else and impossible to find again. The fan club wants one place where fan opinions live, organized and easy to read.\n\nThe fan club has one hard rule: no aggression toward people, and no threats against people or places, may ever go public. Tiradera toward rival clubs (Tigres especially) is welcome; a personal attack never is. The leader is the only safeguard, so nothing may reach readers without his check. The leader knows the basics on a computer and nothing technical, so the admin side has to be simple.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Leader** (role *admin*): one person. Checks and publishes everything, writes the fan club's pages, creates and manages accounts, and puts changes online. Not technical.\n- **Member** (role *editor*): a fan with an account, created by the leader. Writes posts and submits them to the leader; cannot publish, cannot touch pages or accounts.\n- **Reader**: any fan visiting the public site on GitHub Pages, usually on a phone. No account; reads only.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves, per ADR-001:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the leader's computer (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, per ADR-002). Members write there; the leader checks, publishes, manages accounts, and runs the site update. Everything people see is in Spanish.\n- A **public site**: static HTML regenerated from published content only and deployed to GitHub Pages. A home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, a page per post, and the fan club's pages in the menu. Navy-and-white, playful, unmistakably Monterrey, never official.\n\nEvery change readers can see passes through the leader (ADR-003): posts move draft → submitted → published, a member's change to a published post waits as a pending edit, and a member's nickname is chosen once.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login.** The leader and members sign in with email and password and sign out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong email and a wrong password get the same message.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* = the leader: everything. *Editor* = a member: writes, edits and submits their own posts, reads everyone's posts, proposes edits to their own published posts. Editors cannot publish, cannot see or change pages, cannot manage accounts, and cannot run a site update. Enforced on the server for every route, never by hiding links.\n3. **Posts.** A post is a fan's opinion: title, slug, Markdown body, exactly one topic, status (draft, submitted, published), author, and created/updated/published timestamps. Full create, read, update, delete, following the lifecycle below.\n4. **Pages.** Fixed fan-club information: same fields as a post minus the topic, plus a menu-order number. Only the leader creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes and deletes them. Published pages appear in the public menu in menu order.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a content list filterable by status, topic and (leader only) post vs page, and an editor with a *Vista previa* that shows the sanitized result.\n6. **User management.** Leader only: create accounts, change roles, set a nickname, set a new temporary password, deactivate and reactivate. A deactivated user cannot log in, and an existing session stops working on its next request.\n7. **Public site and site update.** `cms publish` regenerates the public site from published posts and pages only, with sanitized Markdown, a menu built from published pages, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The leader's *Actualizar el sitio* button does both.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Leader\n\n1. As the leader, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use the leader's powers.\n2. As the leader, I want a dashboard showing how many posts are waiting for review, so that I know at a glance whether I have checking to do.\n3. As the leader, I want the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts, pending edits, pages and active members, so that I can see the state of the site without opening lists.\n4. As the leader, I want the dashboard to show when the site was last updated, so that I know whether readers are seeing my latest decisions.\n5. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to submitted posts, so that my review queue is one click away.\n6. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to posts with a pending edit, so that I can review changes to published posts.\n7. As the leader, I want to filter the content list by topic and by post vs page, so that I can find things quickly.\n8. As the leader, I want to read a submitted post exactly as readers would see it, so that I can judge whether it crosses from tiradera into a personal attack.\n9. As the leader, I want to publish a submitted post, so that it goes public at the next site update.\n10. As the leader, I want to send back a submitted post to draft, so that its member can rework it.\n11. As the leader, I want to see a pending edit side by side with the published version, so that I can judge exactly what would change.\n12. As the leader, I want to approve a pending edit, so that the improved version replaces the published one.\n13. As the leader, I want to send back a pending edit, so that the published version stays untouched.\n14. As the leader, I want to unpublish a published post, so that it disappears from the public site at the next site update.\n15. As the leader, I want to be stopped from unpublishing a post while a pending edit waits, so that a member's proposed change is never silently thrown away.\n16. As the leader, I want to edit any post directly, so that I can fix a typo without a round trip; my edits to published posts go live at the next site update.\n17. As the leader, I want to write my own posts and publish them directly, so that fan club news does not wait on a review of myself.\n18. As the leader, I want to delete any post after confirming, so that content that should never have existed is gone.\n19. As the leader, I want to create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete pages, so that *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa* and *Cómo unirse* stay accurate.\n20. As the leader, I want to set each page's menu-order number, so that the public menu reads in the order I choose.\n21. As the leader, I want to be prevented from giving a page a name the site already uses (such as the home page or a topic page), so that nothing on the site is overwritten.\n22. As the leader, I want to create a member account with an email, role and temporary password, so that a fan who asked to join can start writing.\n23. As the leader, I want to promote a member to admin or demote an admin to editor, so that I can share the job if I need to.\n24. As the leader, I want to be unable to remove my own admin role or deactivate myself, so that I cannot lock myself out.\n25. As the leader, I want to deactivate an account, so that a member who breaks the house rules can no longer log in.\n26. As the leader, I want to reactivate an account, so that a member can come back.\n27. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's posts to stay up under their nickname, so that the fan club's archive is not broken.\n28. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's submitted posts and pending edits to stay in my queue, so that I still decide what happens to them.\n29. As the leader, I want to change any member's nickname, so that I can fix a nickname that breaks the house rules.\n30. As the leader, I want to set a new temporary password for a member, so that a member who forgot theirs can get back in.\n31. As the leader, I want one *Actualizar el sitio* button that regenerates the public site and uploads it, so that I never need a terminal.\n32. As the leader, I want the button to tell me in plain Spanish what happened at each step, so that I know whether readers can see my changes or what went wrong.\n33. As the leader, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I always know whether my action worked.\n\n### Member\n\n34. As a member, I want to log in with the email and temporary password the leader gave me, so that I can start writing.\n35. As a member, I want to choose my nickname at my first login, so that readers know me by the name I picked.\n36. As a member, I want the site to refuse a nickname someone else already uses, so that nobody can pass as me or I as them.\n37. As a member, I want to change my password on *Mi cuenta*, so that the leader no longer knows it.\n38. As a member, I want to write a post with a title, a topic and a Markdown body, so that I can share my opinion.\n39. As a member, I want the slug to be made from my title, keeping accents and ñ, so that the link reads like my title.\n40. As a member, I want to edit the slug until my post is first published, so that I can tidy the link.\n41. As a member, I want to press *Vista previa* and see exactly what readers will see, so that my formatting is right before I submit.\n42. As a member, I want to save a draft and come back later, so that I can finish a match opinion the next morning.\n43. As a member, I want to submit a finished draft to the leader, so that he knows it is ready to check.\n44. As a member, I want to withdraw a submitted post back to draft, so that I can fix something before the leader reads it.\n45. As a member, I want to delete my own draft, so that I can drop an opinion I changed my mind about.\n46. As a member, I want to propose an edit to my own published post, so that I can correct it while the published version stays up.\n47. As a member, I want my new pending edit to replace my previous one, so that the leader always sees my latest proposal.\n48. As a member, I want to see every post in the content list, including other members', so that I know what has already been written about Saturday's match.\n49. As a member, I want to be refused when I try to change someone else's post or reach a leader screen, so that the rules are real.\n50. As a member, I want a clear \"no tienes permiso\" page when I am refused, so that I understand what happened.\n\n### Reader\n\n51. As a reader, I want a home page with one section per topic showing its three newest posts, so that I can see what fans are saying about each subject.\n52. As a reader, I want a *Ver todos* link on each section, so that I can read every post in a topic.\n53. As a reader, I want each post to show its title, the author's nickname, its topic, and *Publicado el …* (and *Actualizado el …* if it changed after publishing), so that I know who said what and when.\n54. As a reader, I want the menu to list the fan club's pages, so that I can find the house rules and how to join.\n55. As a reader, I want to read *Reglas de la casa*, so that I know where the line between tiradera and a personal attack is.\n56. As a reader, I want *Cómo unirse* to tell me how to ask the leader for an account, so that I can start writing too.\n57. As a reader, I want the site to work on my phone without sideways scrolling, so that I can read it at the stadium.\n58. As a reader, I want links to keep working after I share them on X or Facebook, so that my friends land on the same post.\n59. As a reader, I want to see the disclaimer on every page, so that nobody mistakes the site for an official Rayados site.\n60. As a reader, I never want to see drafts, submitted posts, pending edits, or anything the leader has not approved.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Modules\n\nDeep modules with small interfaces; the web layer stays thin.\n\n- **Accounts.** Password hashing and verification (argon2), login, logout, session handling, loading the current user on every request and rejecting deactivated users, nickname rules, and the user-management operations. Interface: authenticate(email, password) → user or failure; current_user(request); create/update/deactivate/reactivate operations that enforce the self-lockout rules.\n- **Policy.** The single place that answers \"may this person do this action to this item?\" from role, ownership and status. Every write route asks it; templates may use it to hide buttons, but hiding is never the control.\n- **Content.** Posts, pages and pending edits: storage, slug generation, and the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions (table below). Invalid transitions are refused here, not in the routes.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function: Markdown text in, sanitized HTML out (markdown-it-py, then nh3 with an allowlist). Used by *Vista previa*, the leader's review screens and the site export, so the preview is always exactly what readers get.\n- **Site export.** Renders every published post and published page, the topic pages and the home page into an output directory with relative, percent-encoded links. Called by `cms publish` and by the site update.\n- **Site update.** Export, then deploy (push the output to the `gh-pages` branch), then record the time of the last site update. The deploy step is injectable so tests never push. Called by *Actualizar el sitio* and mirrored by the `cms publish` / `cms deploy` CLI.\n- **Admin web layer.** Routes and Spanish templates for login, first-login nickname, *Mi cuenta*, dashboard, content list, post editor, page editor, review screens, users, site update, and the refusal page.\n- **Public templates.** Home, topic page, post page, page, shared layout with menu, topic links and disclaimer.\n- **Seed.** Rebuilds the demo database from scratch with fictional data.\n\n### Data model\n\n- **User**: id, email (unique, used to log in), password hash (argon2), nickname (unique ignoring case; empty until chosen), role (*admin* or *editor*), active flag, created and updated timestamps.\n- **Post**: id, title, slug (unique among posts), Markdown body, topic, status (*draft*, *submitted*, *published*), author (a user), created and updated timestamps, first-published timestamp (set once, never cleared; its presence locks the slug), and an edited-after-publishing timestamp (drives *Actualizado el …*).\n- **Pending edit**: at most one per post; proposed title, topic and Markdown body, created and updated timestamps. The slug is never part of a pending edit.\n- **Page**: id, title, slug (unique among pages, and never a reserved name), Markdown body, status (*draft* or *published*), menu-order number, author, created, updated and first-published timestamps.\n- **Site state**: the time of the last successful export.\n- **Topics** are a fixed list in code, not a table: Match (*Partido*), Lineup (*Alineación*), Coach (*Técnico*), Signings (*Fichajes*), Fan club news (*Noticias del club de aficionados*).\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n| Action | Who | From | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Save | the member who wrote it; the leader | draft | stays draft |\n| Submit | the member who wrote it | draft | submitted |\n| Withdraw | the member who wrote it | submitted | draft |\n| Publish | leader | draft or submitted | published; sets first-published the first time |\n| Send back | leader | submitted | draft |\n| Unpublish | leader | published, with no pending edit | draft |\n| Propose edit | the member who wrote it | published | stays published; creates or replaces its pending edit |\n| Approve | leader | pending edit | the edit replaces title, topic and body; pending edit removed; edited-after-publishing set |\n| Send back (pending edit) | leader | pending edit | pending edit removed; published version untouched |\n| Edit directly | leader | any status | same status; if published, sets edited-after-publishing |\n| Delete | the member who wrote it, drafts only; the leader, any post | any | post and its pending edit removed |\n\nThe leader's own posts may be published straight from draft. A member never changes a submitted or published post directly. A member may read every post in the admin console but act only on their own.\n\nPages have two statuses only (*draft*, *published*) and no submitted step, because only the leader writes them.\n\n### Accounts and access\n\n- Login identifier is the email. The test helper in `tests/conftest.py` already posts `email` and `password` to `/login`; its demo users are updated to match the seed's emails.\n- Wrong email and wrong password both show *\"Correo o contraseña incorrectos.\"*\n- Sessions use a signed, HTTP-only, same-site cookie holding the user id and a CSRF token. The user is reloaded on every request, so deactivation takes effect immediately.\n- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token in a hidden field, including login, logout, *Vista previa* and the site update. A POST without a valid token gets 403.\n- Anonymous requests to any admin route redirect to `/login`. An editor requesting a leader-only route, or acting on someone else's post, gets 403 with a Spanish refusal page that keeps the admin menu. Unknown ids get 404.\n- A user without a nickname is sent to the first-login nickname screen before anything else. Seeded users already have nicknames so the judge's walkthrough is never interrupted.\n- Nickname: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case; afterwards only the leader can change it.\n- Passwords: at least 8 characters when set or changed.\n- The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate themselves. Users are never deleted.\n\n### Admin routes (contract)\n\nPaths and form field names are English; everything people read is Spanish.\n\n- `/login` (GET, POST), `/logout` (POST)\n- `/admin` dashboard; `/admin/nickname` first-login nickname; `/admin/account` *Mi cuenta*\n- `/admin/content` content list with `status`, `topic`, `pending` and (leader only) `type` filters\n- `/admin/posts/new`, `/admin/posts/{id}` and one POST route per lifecycle action, plus a preview POST\n- `/admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit` side-by-side review (leader)\n- `/admin/pages/...` create, edit, publish, unpublish, delete, preview (leader only)\n- `/admin/users/...` list, create, change role, set nickname, set temporary password, deactivate, reactivate (leader only)\n- `/admin/site-update` (POST, leader only)\n\nEvery leader-only route is declared as such in one place, so a test can enumerate all of them.\n\n### Slugs\n\nMade from the title: Unicode-normalized (NFC), lowercased, letters (including á é í ó ú ü ñ) and digits kept, every other run of characters replaced by a single hyphen, trimmed, capped at 80 characters. Example: *\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\"* → `crónica-del-clásico-regio`. A taken slug gets `-2`, `-3`, … A manually entered slug follows the same rules. A post's slug is editable until it is first published, then locked forever, so shared links keep working. Page slugs may not be a reserved name: `index`, `tema`, `posts`, `style`.\n\n### Markdown\n\nRendered with markdown-it-py, then sanitized with nh3 using an allowlist of text-formatting tags, lists, blockquotes, code and links. Scripts, event-handler attributes and `javascript:` links are removed. **Images are removed too**: photo uploads are out of scope and the site must carry no official photos. Links get `rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"`.\n\n### Public site (contract)\n\n- `index.html`: one section per topic in the fixed order, each with its three newest published posts (title, nickname, date) and a *Ver todos* link; a topic with no published posts is hidden on the home page. A Cerro de la Silla banner on top.\n- `tema/<topic-slug>.html`: all published posts in that topic, newest first. All five topic pages are always generated (an empty one says so), so no link ever breaks.\n- `posts/<slug>.html`: title, nickname, topic link, *Publicado el …*, *Actualizado el …* when edited after publishing, and the body.\n- `<page-slug>.html`: a published page.\n- `style.css` at the root.\n- Every page shares a menu (*Inicio* plus published pages by menu order), a row of topic links, and the footer with a stadium silhouette above the disclaimer: *\"Sitio de aficionados. Sin afiliación con el Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"* with *\"Fan site, not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"* beneath.\n- Every `href` and `src` is relative (`../style.css` from nested pages) and percent-encoded, so accented slugs never break a link. File names are written in NFC.\n- The output directory is wiped and regenerated on every export, so unpublished and deleted content disappears.\n- Dates are shown in Spanish (*4 de octubre de 2026*) in Monterrey time, a fixed UTC−6 offset, so no time-zone database is needed.\n\n### Look\n\nNavy and white, with vertical stripes (*rayas*) across the top of every public page, an original Cerro de la Silla silhouette on the home page, and a generic stadium silhouette (not labelled with any sponsor's name) in the footer. All drawings are inline vector graphics written for this site: no crest, logos, photos or image files. Fun to look at, but every page stays readable at 390 px with no horizontal scrolling. The admin console uses the same colors in a calmer, plain layout, with a persistent menu.\n\n### Site update\n\n- `cms publish` exports to `site/`; `cms deploy` pushes `site/` to `gh-pages`. Both keep working exactly as the assignment expects.\n- *Actualizar el sitio* (leader only) runs export then deploy and reports each step, for example *\"Sitio generado ✓ · Subido a GitHub ✓\"*, or a plain Spanish error when the upload fails. A failed upload does not undo a successful export. The dashboard shows the time of the last successful export.\n\n### Configuration\n\nAll secrets and settings come from the environment (`.env`, never committed): secret key, database path, site title (*Club de Aficionados Albiazul*), demo passwords, base path. `.env.example` is updated with the new site title and a `CMS_STUDENT=first-last` placeholder for the transcript hook.\n\n### Demo data (all fictional)\n\nThe seed wipes and rebuilds the database. It creates: the leader and two members, all with fictional nicknames and emails under `albiazul.example`, passwords from the environment; at least one published post in each of the five topics, including an obvious tiradera aimed at Tigres; one draft, one submitted post, and one published post with a pending edit; and the four pages, published, in menu order (*Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*). *Reglas de la casa* spells out the house rules; *Cómo unirse* gives `unete@albiazul.example`. The README lists the demo emails.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check behaviour from the outside**: what a person can do and see through HTTP, and what files the export writes. They never assert on internal function calls, SQL, or template internals.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP interface**, driven through FastAPI's test client against a fresh temporary SQLite database per test, seeded with the test demo users. Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` and the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`. The app factory accepts a database path so tests never touch `cms.db`. A second editor fixture covers ownership rules.\n- **Seam 2: the export output**, generated into a temporary directory and inspected as files and HTML. The deploy step is replaced with a fake that records the call, so no test pushes to GitHub.\n- **Access-control matrix (D3):** a test enumerates every leader-only route from the single declaration and asserts an editor gets 403 and an anonymous visitor is redirected to `/login`. New leader-only routes are covered automatically.\n- **CSRF (D2):** a test replays every POST route without a token and asserts 403.\n- **Sanitizing (D4):** a post containing `<script>` and `onerror=` is checked in *Vista previa* and in the exported page; neither survives.\n- **Drafts never leak (checklist #8):** the export is searched for every draft, submitted post and pending edit; none appears.\n- **Relative paths (F2):** the export is grepped for `href=\"/` and `src=\"/`; every internal link, including an accented slug, resolves to a generated file.\n- **Lifecycle:** every row of the lifecycle table has a test, including the refusals (member publishing, member editing a submitted or published post, unpublishing with a pending edit).\n- **Accounts:** stored passwords start with `$argon2`; wrong password and unknown email give the same message; a deactivated user cannot log in and an open session is rejected; the leader cannot demote or deactivate themselves; nicknames are unique ignoring case.\n- **Persistence (C3):** a post created through one app instance is still there through a new instance on the same database file.\n- **Traceability (E2):** each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one test whose name says which criterion it covers.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and likes; readers only read.\n- Members writing from their own phones or computers. In v1 the admin console runs only on the leader's computer (ADR-001). *Next step, the client's own idea: put only \"write and submit\" online, keep the leader's powers on his computer.*\n- Self sign-up; the leader creates every account.\n- Photo uploads, and images inside posts.\n- Live scores, match statistics, and any integration with Rayados or league data.\n- Multiple clubs or multiple sites.\n- Revision history and rollback (a pending edit is the only stored alternative version).\n- Search, scheduled publishing, per-fan pages, categories or tags beyond the five fixed topics.\n- A bilingual site or a language switch.\n- WYSIWYG editing and drag-and-drop page building (excluded by the assignment).\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Rubric labels:** this spec is the `spec` issue; tickets are labelled `ticket` (core) or `stretch`, each with acceptance criteria and a `Blocked by:` line. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n- **Tracer bullets:** every ticket should cut through model, route, template and test, and be demoable alone. The first tickets should get login, posts and a published post on GitHub Pages as early as possible.\n- **Known trade-off (Q9):** members can read other members' unchecked drafts. Accepted by the client.\n- **Stretch candidates, only after the seven capabilities pass:** revision history with rollback (extends pending edits), switchable theme, live admin deploy.\n- **Deadline:** the Stage 2 grace period ended on 2026-10-07; keep tickets thin.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a69c230d-9797-4496-992b-5eb519787c13","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"543c86f1-4c02-4339-af04-cf127e955eef","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1220b58e-b84f-4b7a-8d23-63036a27aabe","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. {"parentUuid":"92057ffe-c2da-49c1-9106-b56137881721","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu3W3XBBVWuuJSkihZAx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The spec is posted as **issue #1**: https://github.com/maxillamas06-arch/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/1. I also created the `spec`, `ticket`, `stretch` and `ready-for-agent` labels.\n\n## Proposed tickets (8 core)\n\nEach ticket touches the database, a route, a template and tests (B3), and can be shown working on its own.\n\n**T01: The leader and members log in, and members are refused leader screens**\n- *Blocked by:* none\n- *Delivers:*\n  - email + password login and logout; passwords stored as argon2 hashes; the same message for a wrong email or a wrong password\n  - a CSRF token on every form; logged-out visitors sent to `/login`\n  - the Spanish admin layout with its permanent menu\n  - the first leader-only screen (a read-only list of accounts) and the Spanish \"no tienes permiso\" page that members see\n  - leader-only routes declared in one place, plus the test that walks all of them (D3)\n  - seed: the leader and two members, with nicknames\n  - tests: a fresh database for every test\n\n**T02: Members write draft posts and preview them**\n- *Blocked by:* T01\n- *Delivers:*\n  - creating, editing and saving a draft: title, topic, Markdown body, and a slug built from the title with accents kept\n  - **Vista previa**, with scripts, `onerror` and images stripped out\n  - a content list showing every post\n  - members can only edit or delete their own drafts; anyone else's gets a 403\n  - confirmation before deleting, and a success or error message after every save\n\n**T03: The leader publishes a post and it appears on the public site**\n- *Blocked by:* T02\n- *Delivers:*\n  - publish and unpublish, leader only; the slug locks the first time a post is published\n  - `cms publish` builds:\n    - the home page: one section per topic with its newest 3 posts and *Ver todos*\n    - the topic pages\n    - the post pages: nickname, topic, Spanish date\n    - the stripes and the disclaimer\n  - links are relative and encoded; drafts are never exported\n  - deployed live on GitHub Pages\n  - seed: one published post per topic, including the tiradera aimed at Tigres\n\n**T04: Members submit posts and the leader works a review queue**\n- *Blocked by:* T03\n- *Delivers:*\n  - submit, withdraw and send back; the leader publishes from *submitted*\n  - dashboard counts\n  - content list filters by status, topic, and post vs page\n  - seed: one submitted post\n\n**T05: Members propose edits to published posts; the leader approves or sends them back**\n- *Blocked by:* T04\n- *Delivers:*\n  - one pending edit per post, replaced each time the member saves again\n  - a side-by-side review screen; approve or send back\n  - unpublishing is blocked while an edit is waiting\n  - *Actualizado el…* on the public post\n  - a dashboard count and a list filter for pending edits\n  - seed: one pending edit\n\n**T06: The leader manages pages and they appear in the public menu**\n- *Blocked by:* T03\n- *Delivers:*\n  - leader-only creating, editing, publishing, unpublishing and deleting of pages\n  - menu order; reserved names refused\n  - published pages appear in the public menu\n  - seed: the four pages\n\n**T07: The leader manages accounts; members choose a nickname and change their password**\n- *Blocked by:* T01, T03\n- *Delivers:*\n  - creating accounts, changing roles, deactivating and reactivating (any open session stops working)\n  - setting a nickname or a temporary password\n  - the leader can't demote or deactivate himself\n  - a first-login nickname screen, with nicknames unique\n  - **Mi cuenta** for changing your own password\n  - a deactivated member's posts stay up\n\n**T08: The leader updates the site with one button, and the site gets its final look**\n- *Blocked by:* T05, T06, T07\n- *Delivers:*\n  - **Actualizar el sitio**: export, then upload, reporting each step (the upload is faked in tests); the time of the last update on the dashboard\n  - the Cerro de la Silla banner and the stadium footer\n  - a check that the home page and three admin screens fit 390 px\n  - the seed checked against the full spec\n\nEach ticket adds its own demo data to the seed, so `seed_demo.py` runs cleanly at every step (E4).\n\n---\n\n**Questions for you:**\n1. **Does the size feel right?** T03 is the biggest, with publishing, the export and the first deploy all in one. I'd keep it whole, because splitting it leaves a ticket with no database change, and that fails B3.\n2. **Are the blocking edges right?** T06 (pages) and T07 (accounts) only need T03, so they could come in any order after it.\n3. **Should anything be merged or split?**\n\n➡️ **Approve as is.** Eight is inside 7–9, and that leaves room for one `stretch` ticket.\n\n**Something else you need to know:** the two exercises from the manual, `decide()` (Part 4) and `spend()` (Part 5), are still unfinished, and 14 of their tests currently fail. They aren't tickets, but they count for B6 and B7. E1 needs **100%** of the test suite passing for full marks, so they have to get done before you submit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1826,"cache_read_input_tokens":229335,"output_tokens":1890,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":123},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1826,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1890,"cache_read_input_tokens":229335,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1826,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1826},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfu3W2p1e8xyKwqEHjG4q","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:to-tickets","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"6d923b29-2582-495e-9016-7ec5227151d8","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:39:24.994Z","effort":"xhigh","perTurnEffort":"xhigh","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"b6b4744f-5652-4dd5-a4dd-004ff6892799","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfu3dwUm5AMUnihpVLBQK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Q6Fv6fTiSp1XMPdkYKsa8v","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"mkdir -p /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91/scratchpad && cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91/scratchpad/tickets.py <<'PYEOF'\nimport json, re, subprocess, sys\n\nT = [\n(\"T01\", \"T01: The leader and members log in, and members are refused leader screens\", [],\n\"\"\"The leader and members can sign in with email and password and sign out. Anyone not signed in is sent to the login page. Members who try to reach a leader screen see a Spanish \"no tienes permiso\" page. This ticket lays the ground every later ticket stands on: accounts, sessions, CSRF on every form, the Spanish admin layout with its persistent menu, the first leader-only screen (a read-only list of accounts), the single place where leader-only routes are declared, and a fresh test database per test.\"\"\",\n[\n\"The seeded leader and a seeded member can each log in with email and password, land on the dashboard greeted by their nickname, and log out with *Salir*.\",\n\"A wrong password and an unknown email both show *\\\"Correo o contraseña incorrectos.\\\"* and create no session.\",\n\"Stored passwords are argon2 hashes (start with `$argon2`); no plain password is stored or logged.\",\n\"A user whose account is inactive cannot log in.\",\n\"Every POST form carries a CSRF token, including login and logout; a POST without a valid token gets 403.\",\n\"An anonymous request to any admin route redirects to `/login`.\",\n\"The leader sees the list of accounts (email, nickname, role, active); a member requesting it gets 403 and the Spanish refusal page, which keeps the admin menu.\",\n\"Leader-only routes are declared in one place, and a test enumerates all of them asserting member → 403 and anonymous → redirect to `/login`.\",\n\"Every admin page shows the persistent Spanish admin menu.\",\n\"The seed creates the leader and two members (fictional, emails under `albiazul.example`, nicknames set, passwords from the environment) and runs clean from `.env.example` values.\",\n\"`.env.example` sets the site title to *Club de Aficionados Albiazul* and includes a `CMS_STUDENT=first-last` placeholder.\",\n\"Each test runs against its own fresh temporary database; the test helper's demo users match the seed's emails.\",\n]),\n(\"T02\", \"T02: Members write draft posts and preview them\", [\"T01\"],\n\"\"\"A member writes a post (title, one of the five topics, Markdown body), saves it as a draft, comes back to it later, and presses *Vista previa* to see exactly what readers would see. Everyone sees every post in the content list, but a member can change only their own drafts. The leader can edit any post.\"\"\",\n[\n\"A member creates a post with a title, a topic from the fixed five and a Markdown body; it is saved as a draft with that member as author and created/updated timestamps.\",\n\"The slug is generated from the title, NFC-normalized, keeping accents and ñ (*\\\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\\\"* → `crónica-del-clásico-regio`); a taken slug gets `-2`, `-3`, …; it can be edited while the post has never been published; an invalid manual slug is refused with a message.\",\n\"*Vista previa* renders the Markdown below the form without saving; `<script>`, `onerror=` attributes, `javascript:` links and images are removed. The preview POST requires the CSRF token.\",\n\"The content list shows every post from every author with title, topic, nickname, status and last update.\",\n\"A member can open any post read-only but can save or delete only their own drafts; a direct POST to edit or delete another member's post returns 403.\",\n\"The leader can edit any post.\",\n\"Deleting asks for confirmation on a separate step; afterwards the post is gone.\",\n\"Every save, delete and error shows a message.\",\n\"The seed adds one draft written by a member.\",\n]),\n(\"T03\", \"T03: The leader publishes a post and it appears on the public site\", [\"T02\"],\n\"\"\"The leader publishes a post and, after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, readers see it on GitHub Pages: a home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, and a page per post with the author's nickname and a Spanish date, all inside the striped navy-and-white layout with the disclaimer. Drafts never leave the database.\"\"\",\n[\n\"The leader can publish a draft; it becomes published, its first-published time is set, and its slug can no longer be changed.\",\n\"The leader can unpublish a published post back to draft. The leader's own drafts publish directly.\",\n\"Members cannot publish or unpublish: a direct POST returns 403.\",\n\"`uv run cms publish` regenerates `site/` from scratch with: a home page showing one section per topic in fixed order with that topic's three newest published posts (title, nickname, date) and a *Ver todos* link, hiding topics with no published posts; all five topic pages, newest first, an empty one saying so; one page per published post with title, nickname, topic link, *Publicado el …* (Spanish date, Monterrey time UTC−6) and body.\",\n\"Only published posts reach `site/`: a draft's title and body appear nowhere in the output, and a post unpublished since the last export disappears.\",\n\"Markdown in the export is sanitized: a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute exports with neither.\",\n\"Every `href` and `src` in `site/` is relative (no `href=\\\"/` or `src=\\\"/`), and a link to an accented slug is percent-encoded and resolves to a generated file.\",\n\"Every public page has the striped navy-and-white header, a menu with *Inicio*, a row of topic links, and the disclaimer in Spanish with the English line beneath.\",\n\"A post created through one app instance is still there through a new instance on the same database file.\",\n\"The seed adds at least one published post per topic, including an obvious tiradera aimed at Tigres.\",\n\"Manual: the exported site is deployed with `cms deploy` and loads at the GitHub Pages URL over HTTPS.\",\n]),\n(\"T04\", \"T04: Members submit posts and the leader works a review queue\", [\"T03\"],\n\"\"\"A member who has finished a draft submits it to the leader; until the leader acts, the member can withdraw it. The leader works through a review queue: publish, or send back to draft. The dashboard shows the counts, and the content list filters by status and topic.\"\"\",\n[\n\"A member submits their own draft; it becomes submitted. The member can withdraw their own submitted post back to draft.\",\n\"A member cannot edit a submitted post directly (direct POST returns 403); they withdraw it first.\",\n\"The leader can publish a submitted post or send it back to draft.\",\n\"Members cannot send back or publish: direct POSTs return 403.\",\n\"Submitted posts never appear in the export.\",\n\"The dashboard shows counts of drafts, submitted posts (labelled as waiting for review) and published posts.\",\n\"The content list filters by status and by topic.\",\n\"The seed adds one submitted post.\",\n]),\n(\"T05\", \"T05: Members propose edits to published posts; the leader approves or sends them back\", [\"T04\"],\n\"\"\"A member changes their own published post without taking it offline: the change waits as a pending edit while the published version stays public. The leader reviews the two side by side and approves or sends it back. Approved changes show *Actualizado el …* to readers.\"\"\",\n[\n\"A member saving changes to their own published post creates a pending edit (title, topic, body); the published version is unchanged in the admin console and in the export.\",\n\"Saving again replaces the pending edit: a post has at most one.\",\n\"A pending edit never changes the slug.\",\n\"The leader sees the published version and the pending edit side by side. *Approve* replaces title, topic and body, removes the pending edit and marks the post as edited after publishing; the next export shows *Actualizado el …*.\",\n\"*Send back* removes the pending edit and leaves the published version untouched.\",\n\"Unpublishing a post with a pending edit is refused with a message.\",\n\"The leader's direct edit of a published post saves immediately and marks it as edited after publishing.\",\n\"Members cannot approve or send back, and cannot propose edits to another member's post: direct POSTs return 403.\",\n\"Pending edits never appear in the export. Deleting a post deletes its pending edit.\",\n\"The dashboard counts pending edits, and the content list can filter to posts with a pending edit.\",\n\"The seed adds one published post with a pending edit.\",\n]),\n(\"T06\", \"T06: The leader manages pages and they appear in the public menu\", [\"T03\"],\n\"\"\"The leader writes the fan club's own pages (*Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*), orders them, and publishes them. Published pages appear in the public menu on every page. Members never see pages in the admin console.\"\"\",\n[\n\"The leader creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes and deletes pages (title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, menu-order number, author, timestamps); deleting asks for confirmation.\",\n\"Page slugs follow the post slug rules, are unique among pages, and refuse the reserved names `index`, `tema`, `posts`, `style`.\",\n\"The page editor has *Vista previa* using the same sanitizer as posts.\",\n\"Every page route is leader-only and covered by the access-control test; members see no pages in their menu or content list.\",\n\"The export writes each published page at the site root; every public page's menu lists *Inicio* followed by published pages in menu order; draft pages appear nowhere.\",\n\"The leader's content list filters posts vs pages, and the dashboard shows the page count.\",\n\"The seed adds the four pages, published, in menu order; *Reglas de la casa* spells out the house rules and *Cómo unirse* gives `unete@albiazul.example`.\",\n]),\n(\"T07\", \"T07: The leader manages accounts; members choose a nickname and change their password\", [\"T01\", \"T03\"],\n\"\"\"The leader creates accounts for fans who asked to join, changes roles, sets nicknames and temporary passwords, and deactivates or reactivates accounts. A new member chooses their nickname at first login and can change their own password on *Mi cuenta*. The leader can never lock himself out.\"\"\",\n[\n\"The leader creates an account with a unique email, a role and a temporary password of at least 8 characters; the new user has no nickname yet.\",\n\"A user without a nickname is redirected from every admin route to the nickname screen until they choose one: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case. Afterwards a member cannot change it.\",\n\"The leader can change any user's role, set any user's nickname (still unique) and set a new temporary password.\",\n\"The leader can deactivate and reactivate accounts. A deactivated user cannot log in, and an open session of a deactivated user is rejected on its next request.\",\n\"The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate themselves; the attempt is refused with a message.\",\n\"Users are never deleted. A deactivated member's published posts stay in the export under their nickname, and their submitted posts stay in the review queue.\",\n\"On *Mi cuenta* any user changes their own password by giving the current one and a new one of at least 8 characters; it is stored as an argon2 hash.\",\n\"Every user-management route is leader-only and covered by the access-control test.\",\n\"The dashboard shows the number of active members.\",\n]),\n(\"T08\", \"T08: The leader updates the site with one button, and the site gets its final look\", [\"T05\", \"T06\", \"T07\"],\n\"\"\"The leader puts every published change online with one *Actualizar el sitio* button, no terminal needed, and sees in plain Spanish what happened. The public site gets its finished look: a Cerro de la Silla banner on the home page and a stadium silhouette above the disclaimer, readable on a phone.\"\"\",\n[\n\"A leader-only *Actualizar el sitio* POST (with CSRF token) runs the export and then the upload, and reports each step (*\\\"Sitio generado ✓ · Subido a GitHub ✓\\\"*); if the upload fails it shows a plain Spanish error and the successful export still counts.\",\n\"The time of the last successful export is recorded and shown on the dashboard.\",\n\"Tests replace the upload with a fake; no test pushes to GitHub. no image files, crest, logos or photos are used.\",\n\"Manual: no horizontal overflow at 390 px on the public home page, the dashboard, the content list and the post editor.\",\n\"The seed matches the spec's demo data list and runs clean from `.env.example` values.\",\n]),\n]\n\nnums = {}\nfor tid, title, blockers, build, ac in T:\n    blocked = \", \".join(f\"#{nums[b]}\" for b in blockers) if blockers else \"none (can start immediately)\"\n    body = (\n        \"## Parent\\n\\n#1\\n\\n\"\n        f\"## What to build\\n\\n{build}\\n\\n\"\n        \"## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(f\"- [ ] {a}\" for a in ac) + \"\\n\\n\"\n        f\"## Blocked by\\n\\nBlocked by: {blocked}\\n\"\n    )\n    out = subprocess.run([\"gh\", \"issue\", \"create\", \"--title\", title, \"--label\", \"ticket\",\n                          \"--label\", \"ready-for-agent\", \"--body\", body],\n                         capture_output=True, text=True)\n    if out.returncode != 0:\n        print(\"FAILED\", tid, out.stderr); {"parentUuid":"d84c37f8-c070-4b92-a7a6-9d7fed0e62b8","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"03933352-0802-49c2-9adc-c164e080d60c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NpgpRa836M28CkoWFDyCpC","type":"tool_result","content":"git user:  <>\nlast commit author: maxillamas06-arch <maxillamas06@gmail.com>\n--- state\n{\"pct\": 24.0, \"ts\": 1791658238.52383, \"model\": \"Opus 5.5\", \"effort\": \"xhigh\", \"provider\": \"anthropic\", \"five_h\": 28, \"weekly\": 4}\ndocs/process:\n\nnotes:\nclient-brief.md\ncms-field-notes.md\ntoken-budget-plan.md\nusage-ledger.csv\n--- ctx_guard.py\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Stop hook: warn when the context window crosses 50% / 60% / 80%.\n\nClaude Code runs this after every Claude turn (the Stop event) and pipes the\nevent JSON to stdin. It reads the percentage the status line recorded, and\nprints {\"systemMessage\": \"...\"} the first time usage crosses a threshold.\nThe message is shown to YOU, not to Claude. The hook never blocks and never\nruns /compact itself: slash commands are yours to type.\n\nThresholds (override when launching:  CTX_WARN_PCT=1 claude  to test):\n  CTX_WARN_PCT     default 50  -> \"plan a /compact\"\n  CTX_COMPACT_PCT  default 60  -> \"/compact at the next green test\"\n  urgent = CTX_COMPACT_PCT + 20 -> \"compact or /handoff now; consider splitting\"\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nNONE, WARN, COMPACT, URGENT = 0, 1, 2, 3\n\n\ndef thresholds() -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n    warn = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", 50))\n    compact = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_COMPACT_PCT\", 60))\n    return warn, compact, compact + 20\n\n\ndef band_for(pct: float, warn: float, compact: float, urgent: float) -> int:\n    if pct >= urgent:\n        return URGENT\n    if pct >= compact:\n        return COMPACT\n    if pct >= warn:\n        return WARN\n    return NONE\n\n\ndef message_for(band: int, pct: float) -> str:\n    p = f\"{pct:.0f}%\"\n    return {\n        WARN: (\n            f\"Context {p}: finish the current red-green cycle, then plan a \"\n            \"/compact at the next green test.\"\n        ),\n        COMPACT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N \"\n            \"acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"\n        ),\n        URGENT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: compact now (or /handoff and start fresh). If this \"\n            \"ticket keeps overflowing, split it with /to-tickets.\"\n        ),\n    }[band]\n\n\ndef decide(pct: float, last_band: int) -> tuple[str | None, int]:\n    \"\"\"Pure function (unit-tested): return (message or None, band to store).\n\n    Warn once per upward crossing. When usage drops (after /compact or\n    /clear), store the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise A: implement me with /tdd\")\n\nLEDGER_COLUMNS = [\n    \"ts\", \"session\", \"phase\", \"provider\", \"model\", \"effort\",\n    \"ctx_pct\", \"five_h_pct\", \"weekly_pct\",\n]\n\n\ndef log_usage(project: Path, session: str, state: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one row per turn to notes/usage-ledger.csv (rubric item B7).\"\"\"\n    ledger = project / \"notes\" / \"usage-ledger.csv\"\n    phase_file = project / \".claude\" / \"state\" / \"phase\"\n    try:\n        phase = phase_file.read_text().strip() or \"unlabelled\"\n    except OSError:\n        phase = \"unlabelled\"\n\n    def cell(value: object) -> {"parentUuid":"d833e853-10ad-46a1-8f51-7c6d29d99523","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"03933352-0802-49c2-9adc-c164e080d60c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. name: null | login: maxillamas06-arch\n--- test_ctx_guard\n\"\"\"Tests for the context-threshold hooks (IPHS 400 MP2, setup exercise).\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport json\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHOOKS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / \".claude\" / \"hooks\"\n\n\ndef load(name):\n    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, HOOKS / f\"{name}.py\")\n    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n    return mod\n\n\nguard = load(\"ctx_guard\")\n\n\ndef run(script, payload, project, **env):\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, str(HOOKS / script)],\n        input=json.dumps(payload),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        env={**os.environ, \"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\": str(project), **env},\n    )\n\n\n# ---- pure logic -----------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_silent_below_50():\n    assert guard.decide(49.9, guard.NONE) == (None, guard.NONE)\n\n\ndef test_warns_once_at_50():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(52, guard.NONE)\n    assert band == guard.WARN and \"52%\" in msg\n    assert guard.decide(55, band) == (None, guard.WARN)  # no nagging\n\n\ndef test_compact_message_at_60_names_focus_note():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(61, guard.WARN)\n    assert band == guard.COMPACT and \"/compact keep:\" in msg\n\n\ndef test_urgent_at_80_suggests_split():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(81, guard.COMPACT)\n    assert band == guard.URGENT and \"/to-tickets\" in msg\n\n\ndef test_rearms_after_compaction():\n    _, band = guard.decide(20, guard.COMPACT)   # usage dropped after /compact\n    assert band == guard.NONE\n    msg, _ = guard.decide(51, band)             # next crossing warns again\n    assert msg is not None\n\n\ndef test_thresholds_from_env(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", \"1\")\n    msg, _ = guard.decide(2, guard.NONE)\n    assert msg is not None\n\n\n# ---- end to end: status line -> Stop hook ---------------------------------\n\ndef test_statusline_then_stop_hook(tmp_path):\n    sl = run(\"ctx_statusline.py\",\n             {\"session_id\": \"s1\", \"model\": {\"display_name\": \"Opus\"},\n              \"context_window\": {\"used_percentage\": 63.4}}, tmp_path)\n    assert \"ctx 63%\" in sl.stdout\n    out = run(\"ctx_guard.py\", {\"session_id\": \"s1\", \"hook_event_name\": \"Stop\"}, tmp_path)\n    assert out.returncode == 0\n    assert \"/compact\" in json.loads(out.stdout)[\"systemMessage\"]\n    again = run(\"ctx_guard.py\", {\"session_id\": \"s1\", \"hook_event_name\": \"Stop\"}, tmp_path)\n    assert again.stdout.strip() == \"\"           # warned once, then quiet\n\n\ndef test_stop_hook_silent_without_data(tmp_path):\n    out = run(\"ctx_guard.py\", {\"session_id\": \"nobody\"}, tmp_path)\n    assert out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_stop_hook_survives_garbage_stdin(tmp_path):\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HOOKS / \"ctx_guard.py\")],\n                         input=\"not json\", capture_output=True, text=True,\n                         env={**os.environ, \"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\": str(tmp_path)})\n    assert out.returncode == 0\n\n\ndef test_precompact_logs_focus_note(tmp_path):\n    run(\"ctx_compact_log.py\",\n        {\"session_id\": \"abcdef123\", \"trigger\": \"manual\",\n         \"custom_instructions\": \"keep: ticket #5 criteria\"}, tmp_path)\n    log = (tmp_path / {"parentUuid":"8972e96b-ba98-410f-bf36-2236db5db102","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"03933352-0802-49c2-9adc-c164e080d60c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KDvoGLeyLdbzqsvd2bYYBi","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\n\nUsage:\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # summary + forecast\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py --remaining 4   # 4 tickets still to do\n\nWhy positive deltas: the 5-hour and weekly meters RESET (drop to 0) when their\nwindow rolls over, and the weekly one only ever climbs inside a week. Summing\nonly the increases between consecutive rows measures what you actually spent\nand ignores the resets. That is what spend() does, and it is your exercise.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nLEDGER = Path(\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\")\n\n\ndef spend(series: list[float | None]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Total rise across a meter that can reset to a lower value.\n\n    Sum every increase between consecutive readings; ignore blanks (None) and\n    any drop, which means the window reset.\n\n    >>> spend([10.0, 12.0, 15.0])\n    5.0\n    >>> spend([80.0, 5.0, 9.0])\n    4.0\n    >>> spend([None, 4.0, None, 7.0])\n    3.0\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise B: implement me with /tdd\")\n\ndef read_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    with path.open(newline=\"\") as f:\n        return list(csv.DictReader(f))\n\n\ndef to_float(text: str | None) -> float | None:\n    try:\n        return float(text) if text not in (None, \"\") else None\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\ndef by_phase(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    phases: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(\n        lambda: {\"turns\": 0, \"five\": [], \"weekly\": [], \"models\": set(), \"providers\": set()}\n    )\n    for row in rows:\n        phase = phases[row.get(\"phase\") or \"unlabelled\"]\n        phase[\"turns\"] += 1\n        phase[\"five\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"five_h_pct\")))\n        phase[\"weekly\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"weekly_pct\")))\n        if row.get(\"model\"):\n            phase[\"models\"].add(row[\"model\"])\n        if row.get(\"provider\"):\n            phase[\"providers\"].add(row[\"provider\"])\n    return phases\n\n\ndef ticket_phases(phases: dict[str, dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return sorted(p for p in phases if p.upper().startswith(\"T\") and p[1:].isdigit())\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--ledger\", type=Path, default=LEDGER)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--remaining\", type=int, default=0, help=\"tickets not yet built\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    if not args.ledger.exists():\n        raise SystemExit(f\"No ledger at {args.ledger}. Is the Stop hook registered?\")\n    rows = read_rows(args.ledger)\n    if not rows:\n        raise SystemExit(\"Ledger is empty.\")\n    phases = by_phase(rows)\n\n    print(f\"{'phase':<14}{'turns':>6}{'5h spent':>10}{'weekly':>9}  models / provider\")\n    for name, data in sorted(phases.items()):\n        mix = \",\".join(sorted(data[\"models\"])) or \"?\"\n        prov = \",\".join(sorted(data[\"providers\"] - {\"anthropic\"}))\n        print(f\"{name:<14}{data['turns']:>6}{spend(data['five']):>9.1f}%\"\n              f\"{spend(data['weekly']):>8.1f}%  {mix}{(' @' + prov) if prov else ''}\")\n\n    tickets = ticket_phases(phases)\n    if tickets:\n        per = sum(spend(phases[t][\"weekly\"]) for t in tickets) / len(tickets)\n        print(f\"\\nTickets done: {len(tickets)} · average weekly cost per ticket: {per:.1f}%\")\n        last = next((to_float(r.get(\"weekly_pct\")) for r in reversed(rows)\n                     if to_float(r.get(\"weekly_pct\")) is not None), None)\n        if last is not None and args.remaining:\n            need, headroom = per * args.remaining, 100 - last\n            verdict = \"FITS\" if need <= headroom * 0.8 else \"TIGHT\" if need <= headroom else \"OVER BUDGET\"\n            print(f\"Forecast: {args.remaining} tickets need ~{need:.0f}% of the weekly cap; \"\n                  f\"{headroom:.0f}% remains → {verdict}\")\n            if verdict != \"FITS\":\n                print(\"Fix in this order: 1) lower effort  2) switch to Sonnet/Haiku  \"\n                      \"3) /clear more often  4) split fat tickets  5) Plan B backend (declare it)\")\n    else:\n        print(\"\\nNo ticket phases yet. Write the ticket id into .claude/state/phase \"\n              \"at the start of each /implement session.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n--- tests\n\"\"\"Tests for the token-budget report (IPHS 400 MP2, exercise 2).\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nspec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\"usage_report\", ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"usage_report.py\")\nur = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\nspec.loader.exec_module(ur)\n\nHEADER = \"ts,session,phase,provider,model,effort,ctx_pct,five_h_pct,weekly_pct\\n\"\n\n\ndef ledger(tmp_path, *rows):\n    p = tmp_path / \"usage-ledger.csv\"\n    p.write_text(HEADER + \"\".join(rows))\n    return p\n\n\ndef row(phase, five, weekly, model=\"Sonnet\", provider=\"anthropic\"):\n    return f\"2026-09-30T10:00:00Z,abc,{phase},{provider},{model},medium,40.0,{five},{weekly}\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_spend_counts_only_increases():\n    assert ur.spend([10.0, 12.0, 15.0]) == 5.0\n\n\ndef test_spend_ignores_window_reset():\n    assert ur.spend([80.0, 5.0, 9.0]) == 4.0\n\n\ndef test_spend_skips_blanks():\n    assert ur.spend([None, 4.0, None, 7.0]) == 3.0\n\n\ndef test_spend_empty_is_zero():\n    assert ur.spend([]) == 0.0 and ur.spend([None, None]) == 0.0\n\n\ndef test_report_groups_by_phase(tmp_path):\n    p = ledger(tmp_path, row(\"grill\", 5, 2, model=\"Opus\"), row(\"grill\", 15, 6, model=\"Opus\"),\n               row(\"T01\", 20, 8), row(\"T01\", 30, 12))\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts/usage_report.py\"),\n                          \"--ledger\", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert \"grill\" in out.stdout and \"10.0%\" in out.stdout   # 5 -> 15\n    assert \"Opus\" in out.stdout\n    assert \"average weekly cost per ticket: 4.0%\" in out.stdout\n\n\ndef test_forecast_flags_over_budget(tmp_path):\n    p = ledger(tmp_path, row(\"T01\", 10, 60), row(\"T01\", 40, 80))\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts/usage_report.py\"),\n                          \"--ledger\", str(p), \"--remaining\", \"4\"], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert \"OVER BUDGET\" in out.stdout and \"split fat tickets\" in out.stdout\n\n\ndef test_missing_ledger_explains(tmp_path):\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts/usage_report.py\"),\n                          \"--ledger\", str(tmp_path / \"nope.csv\")], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert out.returncode != 0 and \"Stop hook\" in out.stderr\n\n\ndef test_backup_provider_shown(tmp_path):\n    p = ledger(tmp_path, row(\"T05\", 0, 10, model=\"glm-5.3\", provider=\"api.z.ai\"),\n               row(\"T05\", 5, 14, model=\"glm-5.3\", provider=\"api.z.ai\"))\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts/usage_report.py\"),\n                          \"--ledger\", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert \"@api.z.ai\" in out.stdout\n--- ledger\nts,session,phase,provider,model,effort,ctx_pct,five_h_pct,weekly_pct\r\n2026-10-10T17:24:53Z,9a7f3e0c,grill,anthropic,Opus 5.5,xhigh,11.0,7,1\r\n2026-10-10T17:25:57Z,9a7f3e0c,grill,anthropic,Opus 5.5,xhigh,11.0,8,1\r\n2026-10-10T17:30:01Z,9a7f3e0c,grill,anthropic,Opus 5.5,xhigh,12.0,9,1\r\n2026-10-10T17:31:01Z,9a7f3e0c,grill,anthropic,Opus 5.5,xhigh,12.0,9,1\r\n      32 notes/usage-ledger.csv","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"5d8cf4aa-7b6e-4cae-a099-61e9640ae9fd","timestamp":"2026-10-10T18:51:06.139Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\n\nUsage:\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # It reads the percentage the status line recorded, and\nprints {\"systemMessage\": \"...\"} the first time usage crosses a threshold.\nThe message is shown to YOU, not to Claude. The hook never blocks and never\nruns /compact itself: slash commands are yours to type.\n\nThresholds (override when launching:  CTX_WARN_PCT=1 claude  to test):\n  CTX_WARN_PCT     default 50  -> \"plan a /compact\"\n  CTX_COMPACT_PCT  default 60  -> \"/compact at the next green test\"\n  urgent = CTX_COMPACT_PCT + 20 -> \"compact or /handoff now; consider splitting\"\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nNONE, WARN, COMPACT, URGENT = 0, 1, 2, 3\n\n\ndef thresholds() -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n    warn = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", 50))\n    compact = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_COMPACT_PCT\", 60))\n    return warn, compact, compact + 20\n\n\ndef band_for(pct: float, warn: float, compact: float, urgent: float) -> int:\n    if pct >= urgent:\n        return URGENT\n    if pct >= compact:\n        return COMPACT\n    if pct >= warn:\n        return WARN\n    return NONE\n\n\ndef message_for(band: int, pct: float) -> str:\n    p = f\"{pct:.0f}%\"\n    return {\n        WARN: (\n            f\"Context {p}: finish the current red-green cycle, then plan a \"\n            \"/compact at the next green test.\"\n        ),\n        COMPACT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N \"\n            \"acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"\n        ),\n        URGENT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: compact now (or /handoff and start fresh). If this \"\n            \"ticket keeps overflowing, split it with /to-tickets.\"\n        ),\n    }[band]\n\n\ndef decide(pct: float, last_band: int) -> tuple[str | None, int]:\n    \"\"\"Pure function (unit-tested): return (message or None, band to store).\n\n    Warn once per upward crossing. When usage drops (after /compact or\n    /clear), store the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise A: implement me with /tdd\")\n\nLEDGER_COLUMNS = [\n    \"ts\", \"session\", \"phase\", \"provider\", \"model\", \"effort\",\n    \"ctx_pct\", \"five_h_pct\", \"weekly_pct\",\n]\n\n\ndef log_usage(project: Path, session: str, state: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one row per turn to notes/usage-ledger.csv (rubric item B7).\"\"\"\n    ledger = project / \"notes\" / \"usage-ledger.csv\"\n    phase_file = project / \".claude\" / \"state\" / \"phase\"\n    try:\n        phase = phase_file.read_text().strip() or \"unlabelled\"\n    except OSError:\n        phase = \"unlabelled\"\n\n    def cell(value: object) -> str:\n        return \"\" if value is None else str(value)\n\n    row = [\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"),\n        session[:8], phase, cell(state.get(\"provider\")), cell(state.get(\"model\")),\n        cell(state.get(\"effort\")), f\"{float(state.get('pct', 0)):.1f}\",\n        cell(state.get(\"five_h\")), cell(state.get(\"weekly\")),\n    ]\n    try:\n        ledger.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        new = not ledger.exists()\n        with ledger.open(\"a\", newline=\"\") as f:\n            writer = csv.writer(f)\n            if new:\n                writer.writerow(LEDGER_COLUMNS)\n            writer.writerow(row)\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    session = event.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    ctx_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\"\n    band_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}_band.json\"\n\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(ctx_file.read_text())\n        pct = float(state[\"pct\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        return  # no status-line data yet: stay silent\n    try:\n        last_band = int(json.loads(band_file.read_text())[\"band\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        last_band = NONE\n\n    log_usage(project, session, state)\n\n    msg, band = decide(pct, last_band)\n    try:\n        band_file.write_text(json.dumps({\"band\": band}))\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n    if msg:\n        print(json.dumps({\"systemMessage\": msg}))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass  # a warning hook must never break the session\n    sys.exit(0)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":64,"oldLines":7,"newStart":64,"newLines":10,"lines":["     Warn once per upward crossing.
